purpose: THE fee & estimate MASTER LIST — every configuration item the fee/estimate/payment engine can hold, mapped to the canonical rules-library concepts, with an AUTO-DERIVED per-state status to be verified/filled by the step-2 gap pass. Statuses: value_present · value_present+delegation · delegated_to_regulation_or_schedule · defers_to_city · actual_cost_or_reasonable · rule_without_value · silent.

sources.engine: backend/src/services/feeEngine.js, frontend FeeConfigPage DEFAULT_CONFIG, paymentClockPolicy.FIELDS, feeWaiverPolicy.FIELDS

known_holes: NJ: dictionary lists NJ under several fee concepts but the pruned corpus holds ZERO NJ rules (chunked-discovery failure) — every NJ cell is "silent" here and must be re-researched.
Delegations: where a statute delegates rate-setting to a regulation / AG rule / uniform schedule (TX 1 TAC §70.3 pattern), the regulation text is NOT in the corpus — the gap pass follows those.

Duplicated homes: estimate threshold, deposit threshold and deposit cap live in BOTH fee_profiles.requestRules and jurisdiction_rules fee_waiver.* — one concept, two stores; a later step picks one home.
Not in engine: per-requestor periodic free hours (TX §552.275), repeat/aggregation rules — recorded here so the field can exist before anyone populates it.

AL.snippet: A public officer may require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before the requester may receive any public records (standard request); more generally, a certified copy is furnished on paymen

verified.source_language: The public officer may require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before the requester may receive any public records. If the public officer elects to charge a fee, the public officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment. The requester may opt not to pay the fee and thus not receive any substantive response. Additionally, the public officer shall have the discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records. | § 36-12-41: Every public officer having custody of a public record that a resident has a right to inspect shall provide him or her, on proper request as provided in this article, with a copy of the public record, on payment of a reasonable fee, as further provided in this article.
verified.effective_status: Current; Act 2024-278 effective October 1, 2024; no amendment to the fee provisions in the 2025 or 2026 Regular Sessions (codified history through Act 2026-592 shows only Act 2024-278)
verified.notes: No statewide per-page rate or ceiling for municipalities; the operative standard is 'a reasonable fee set by the public officer' (standard request: may charge; time-intensive request: shall charge). Article applies to every 'public officer' (state, county, municipal) except the judicial branch/Art. VI offices (§ 36-12-40(b)). Agency regime (does NOT bind municipalities): Governor's Executive Order No. 734 §4 caps state executive-branch agency fees (up to $20.00/hour incl. $20 minimum for retrieval/preparation; no charge for legal review/redaction; up to $0.50/page for 8.5x11 paper copies; no per-page fee for electronic delivery; actual costs with advance notice) — recorded as AL-9006..AL-9008. Official link is the Legislature's Code of Alabama viewer (browse Title 36 > Chapter 12 > Article 3; section text also served by its GraphQL endpoint https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql, query codeOfAlabamaSection); alternate direct text: enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF.

AZ.snippet: The custodian may charge a fee for furnishing copies, printouts or photographs if the facilities are available; the statute sets no rate.

verified.source_authority: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 39-121.01(D)(1); Ariz. Att'y Gen. Op. I13-012 (R13-018); Ariz. Att'y Gen. Agency Handbook § 6.5.5
verified.source_language: The custodian of such records shall promptly furnish such copies, printouts or photographs and may charge a fee if the facilities are available, except that public records for purposes listed in section 39-122 or 39-127 shall be furnished without charge.
verified.effective_status: Amended effective September 26, 2025 (Laws 2025, ch. 102, SB 1372, approved May 2, 2025; general effective date of the 57th Leg., 1st Reg. Sess.) — codified text opened at azleg.gov 2026-08-19
verified.notes: Statute is a bare Permission ('may charge a fee if the facilities are available') with no per-page number and no rulemaking delegation; the custodian (for a city, the city) sets the rate. AG guidance frames the permissible non-commercial fee as one that offsets copying costs, 'including a reasonable amount for the cost of time, equipment, and personnel used in producing copies of records, but not for costs of searching for the records' (AZ-9004). No graduated bands, no free pages. 2026 SB 1437 ('material costs only') and HB 2139 ('reasonable fee') were not enacted.

CA.snippet: Fees for copies of records are limited to fees covering the direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if one applies.

verified.value: direct costs of duplication
verified.unit: USD per page (city sets under the standard)
verified.source_language: Except with respect to public records exempt from disclosure by express provisions of law, each state or local agency, upon a request for a copy of records that reasonably describes an identifiable record or records, shall make the records promptly available to any person upon payment of fees covering direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if applicable. Upon request, an exact copy shall be provided unless impracticable to do so.
verified.effective_status: Current (added Stats. 2021, ch. 614 (AB 473), operative Jan. 1, 2023; no amendment 2024–2026 as of 2026-08-19)
verified.notes: No statewide cents-per-page figure for general municipal records; the standard is 'direct costs of duplication' (judicially glossed as the cost of running the copy machine and conceivably the operator, excluding retrieval/inspection/handling — CA-9003). 'Or a statutory fee if applicable' points to record-specific statutes; the only general-application one binding city clerks found is Gov. Code § 81008 (Political Reform Act statements ≤ $0.10/page, CA-9009). Counties (not cities) have separate authority under Gov. Code § 54985 to set copy fees at reasonable cost per 85 Ops.Cal.Atty.Gen. 225 (2002) (located, not opened). Applies to 'each state or local agency' — no separate state-agency schedule.

CO.snippet: The custodian may charge a fee not to exceed twenty-five cents per standard page for a copy of a public record.

verified.source_language: A custodian may charge a fee not to exceed twenty-five cents per standard page for a copy of a public record or a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing a copy, printout, or photograph of a public record in a format other than a standard page; except that a custodian shall not charge a per-page fee for providing records in a digital or electronic format.
verified.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
verified.notes: Ceiling, not a value: 'may charge a fee not to exceed twenty-five cents per standard page'. Binds every custodian incl. cities/towns (political subdivisions). Per-page fee prohibited for digital/electronic format (CO-9002). 'Standard page' is not defined in statute.

CT.snippet: For all public agencies other than state offices/agencies, the fee for a copy of a public record shall not exceed fifty cents per page.

verified.unit: USD per page (one side of a piece of printed matter, 108 CA 471) — paper copy by a municipal or other non-state public agency
verified.source_language: The fee for any copy provided in accordance with the Freedom of Information Act: (B) By all other public agencies, as defined in section 1-200, shall not exceed fifty cents per page. If any copy provided in accordance with said Freedom of Information Act requires a transcription, or if any person applies for a transcription of a public record, the fee for such transcription shall not exceed the cost thereof to the public agency.
verified.effective_status: Current — Gen. Stat. rev. to Jan. 1, 2025; § 1-212 not in the 2026 Supplement (rev. to Jan. 1, 2026 — only § 1-210(b)(17) amended in 2025); last amended P.A. 12-205; 2026-session public acts (through P.A. 26-68) searched — none amend § 1-212
verified.notes: 'Shall not exceed fifty cents per page' — a ceiling, not a set rate; the city sets its per-page fee at or below $0.50. State offices/agencies are capped at $0.25 (§ 1-212(a)(A), CT-0016; FOIC FAQ: 'Municipal agencies may charge a maximum of fifty cents per page and state agencies may charge a maximum of twenty-five cents per page'). Per FOIC FIC 2025-0213 ¶¶ 35-37 the per-page fee is the ONLY chargeable fee for paper records (no labor/handling add-ons). Town clerks' recorded/filed documents carry a separate $1/page statutory fee (§ 7-34a, CT-9002). No 2024-2026 amendment.

FL.snippet: For duplicated copies of records not larger than 14 by 8.5 inches, the agency may charge up to 15 cents per one-sided copy.

verified.unit: USD per one-sided duplicated copy, page not more than 14 x 8.5 inches (two-sided: no more than an additional 0.05)
verified.source_language: The custodian of public records shall furnish a copy or a certified copy of the record upon payment of the fee prescribed by law. If a fee is not prescribed by law, the following fees are authorized: (a)1. Up to 15 cents per one-sided copy for duplicated copies of not more than 14 inches by 8 1/2 inches; 2. No more than an additional 5 cents for each two-sided copy; and
verified.effective_status: Current (2025 Florida Statutes; s. 119.07 last amended s. 1, ch. 2021-173; no 2024, 2025 or 2026 amendment to subsection (4) — CS/HB 437 (2026), which would have restricted fees, authorized waivers and required written cost estimates, passed the House 111-0 on 3/4/2026 and died in Senate Rules 3/13/2026)
verified.notes: Ceiling under a Permission ('up to 15 cents'); city sets the operative rate at or below. Applies 'if a fee is not prescribed by law' — other statutes may prescribe fees for particular records (e.g., s. 28.24 clerks of court; not municipal). 'Duplicated copies' = s. 119.011(7)/s. 283.30 (electrophotographic/xerographic/laser/offset). Binds every 'agency' incl. municipal officers/units (s. 119.011(2)).

GA.snippet: In addition to labor charges, an agency may charge for copying, not to exceed 10 cents per page for letter or legal size documents, or the actual cost of producing the copy for other document types.

verified.unit: USD per page (letter or legal size)
verified.source_language: In addition to a charge for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records, an agency may charge a fee for the copying of records or data, not to exceed 10¢ per page for letter or legal size documents or, in the case of other documents, the actual cost of producing the copy.
verified.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
verified.notes: Statutory cap; city sets the operative per-page value at or under 10¢ for letter/legal pages. Operative verb is 'may charge ... not to exceed' (Permission with ceiling); GA-9001 amends GA-0018's rule_type from Requirement to Permission and cleans a stray '$0.25' remark in its notes. 'Agency' (§ 50-18-70(b)(1) via § 50-14-1(a)(1)(B)-(C)) includes every county, municipal corporation, school district and their departments, so the figure binds municipalities directly; Georgia runs a single regime for state and local bodies.

ID.snippet: The fee charged to a resident may not exceed the actual cost to the agency of copying the record.

verified.value: actual cost to the agency of copying the record (resident); actual costs of the public agency (nonresident)
verified.unit: USD per page (city-set under the standard)
verified.source_language: A public agency or public official may establish separate copying fee schedules for requests submitted by residents and requests submitted by persons who are not residents. The fee for residents may not exceed the actual cost to the agency of copying the record if another fee is not otherwise provided by law. | Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, a public agency or public official may charge fees for labor and copying costs associated with locating and copying documents requested by a person who is not a resident or an employee of a resident. The fee rates and schedule for requests made by persons who are not residents or employees of residents shall be at the discretion of the public agency or public official as long as such fees do not exceed actual costs of the public agency or public official.
verified.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
verified.notes: Idaho sets no cents-per-page figure. Two regimes: residents (§ 74-101(15)) — fee may not exceed actual cost of copying, and the first 100 paper pages are free (ID-0018); nonresidents — rate and schedule at agency discretion, not to exceed actual costs. 'Public agency' = state or local agency (§ 74-101(8),(11)), so the standard binds cities directly. AG Legal Guideline 1/25/1993 (ID-9012): a city may not by ordinance charge above actual cost. City fee adoption is subject to the § 63-1311A hearing/notice procedure for new fees or >5% increases (applicability note). Statutes updated 7/1/2026 show no 2026 change.

IL.snippet: The fee for black-and-white, letter- or legal-sized copies (after the free 50) may not exceed 15 cents per page.

verified.unit: USD per page (black-and-white, letter or legal size, pages beyond the first 50)
verified.source_language: The fee for black and white, letter or legal sized copies shall not exceed 15 cents per page. No fees shall be charged for the first 50 pages of black and white, letter or legal sized copies requested by a requester.
verified.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
verified.notes: 'Public body' (5 ILCS 140/2(a)) expressly includes cities, villages and incorporated towns, so the 15-cent ceiling binds municipalities directly. The city sets its operative rate at or below the ceiling in the 'standard scale of fees, established and made public' (IL-9002) and must post 'any fees allowable under Section 6' (Sec. 4(b)). Outer bound remains actual cost of reproduction (IL-9001). Per PAC binding opinion 25-015 (Dec. 23, 2025, summarized in PAC Update Winter 2026) the 15-cent fee is available only when the records are maintained in paper format; records maintained electronically are limited to the recording-medium cost (IL-0031, IL-9013).

IN.snippet: The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of ten cents ($0.10) per non-color page or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per color page, or the agency's actual cost.

verified.unit: USD per page (non-color), or the agency's actual cost of copying if greater (actual cost = paper + per-page equipment cost only; no labor or overhead)
verified.source_language: This subsection applies to a public agency that is not a state agency. The fiscal body (as defined in IC 36-1-2-6) of the public agency, or the governing body, if there is no fiscal body, shall establish a fee schedule for the certification or copying of documents. The fee for certification of documents may not exceed five dollars ($5) per document. The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of: (1) ten cents ($0.10) per page for copies that are not color copies or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for color copies; or (2) the actual cost to the agency of copying the document. As used in this subsection, "actual cost" means the cost of paper and the per-page cost for use of copying or facsimile equipment and does not include labor costs or overhead costs. A fee established under this subsection must be uniform throughout the public agency and uniform to all purchasers.
verified.effective_status: Current — subsection unchanged since P.L. 58-2016 per the handbook history line and quoted identically in PAC advisory opinions issued through August 2026; HEA 1360 (P.L. 97-2026, eff. July 1, 2026) added (n)-(o) without altering this text per PAC's Statutory Additions summary. Codified iga.in.gov copy not opened (site inaccessible 2026-08-19).
verified.notes: Local regime: the fiscal body (city/town council) 'shall establish a fee schedule' by ordinance; the schedule may not exceed the greater of $0.10/page (non-color) or actual cost as narrowly defined. PAC opinions (19-FC-67, 21-FC-1, 22-FC-145) treat $0.10 as the practical cap for standard-size B&W copies and reject flat per-report fees. State-agency regime differs: § 8(c) IDOA uniform copying fee (≤ greater of average cost or $0.10). Text opened in PAC opinion 25-FC-326 (July 21, 2026) and PAC Handbook p. 52; identical in 19-FC-67. Note: HEA 1360 (2026) § 8(n) permits a supplemental fee ≤ $0.25/page for non-Indiana requesters (IN-9007).

KS.snippet: Fees for copies shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available.

verified.source_language: Except as provided by subsection (h) or where fees for inspection or for copies of a public record are prescribed by statute, each public agency may prescribe reasonable fees for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to the following: … In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records.
verified.effective_status: Amended effective 2025-07-01 (L. 2025, ch. 89, § 1 [HB 2134]); no 2026 amendment
verified.notes: No statewide per-page rate for municipalities. Standard = 'reasonable fees' capped at 'the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time'; incidental non-attributable costs excluded. The city supplies the per-page value under this ceiling. AG Op. 87-4 (1987) found a school district's 20-cents-per-page fee 'not unreasonable' because it reflected documented actual cost — a fact-specific finding, not a statewide figure. The $.25/page 'deemed reasonable' safe harbor at K.S.A. 45-240(c) applies ONLY to not-for-profit entities receiving public funds, not to public agencies. State-agency practice (NOT binding on municipalities): Dept. of Administration KORA page charges $0.25/page copies after 1 hour of staff time or 100 pages (EO 18-05, residents), staff time at rate of pay (attorney $60/hr, clerical $18/hr, IT $38/hr), mailing $0.50 first 5 pages/$0.25 per additional 5 pages, fax $0.65 per 10 pages; Secretary of State: $0.25/page paper, $0.125/page electronic, clerical $21/hr, attorney $52/hr, IT $42/hr, estimate must be prepaid, $30 returned-check fee. These are single-agency policies under K.S.A. 45-219(c)(7) ('established ... by the agency head'), not a uniform state schedule.

LA.snippet: The custodian may establish and collect reasonable fees for making copies of public records.

verified.source_language: The custodian may establish and collect reasonable fees for making copies of public records, which may include the transmission of electronic copies of public records.
verified.effective_status: Current (last amended Acts 2024, No. 411; fee text of (C)(1)(a) as amended by Acts 2023, No. 247, eff. Aug. 1, 2023; no 2025 or 2026 amendment found)
verified.notes: Standard term: 'reasonable fees for making copies'. No statutory number for non-state-agency custodians (municipalities); the custodian who elects to charge must adopt and post a reasonable fee schedule (LA-0022). AG Op. 15-0056 (LA-9010): a reasonable fee 'does include, at a minimum, the actual costs for making the copies' and is not to recoup generation cost. State-agency regime (NOT binding on cities): LAC 4:I.301.B sets a $0.25/page minimum for paper copies up to 8.5x14 (LA-9002) — usable only as guidance/reference. 2026 RS SB 493 (20 free pages, 5c/page cap) was withdrawn 4/22/2026 and is not law.

MA.snippet: The fee for standard black-and-white paper copies or printouts shall not exceed 5 cents per page, for both single- and double-sided copies.

MI.snippet: The charge for paper copies must not exceed 10 cents per sheet for copies made on 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 paper, calculated as a total cost per sheet.

MN.snippet: For requests of 100 or fewer black-and-white letter/legal-size paper copies, actual costs may not be used; the entity may charge no more than 25 cents per page copied.

MO.snippet: Fees for copying public records provided in paper form shall not exceed ten cents per page for a paper copy not larger than nine by fourteen inches.

NC.snippet: An agency may not charge a fee for an uncertified copy of a public record that exceeds the actual cost to the agency of making the copy.

verified.value: actual cost to the public agency of making the copy
verified.unit: USD per page (ceiling: actual cost; 'actual cost' = direct, chargeable reproduction costs per GAAP, excluding costs the agency would have incurred anyway)
verified.rule_type: Prohibition (fee may not exceed actual cost)
verified.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, no public agency shall charge a fee for an uncertified copy of a public record that exceeds the actual cost to the public agency of making the copy. For purposes of this subsection, "actual cost" is limited to direct, chargeable costs related to the reproduction of a public record as determined by generally accepted accounting principles and does not include costs that would have been incurred by the public agency if a request to reproduce a public record had not been made.
verified.effective_status: Current (ncleg.gov General Statutes current through S.L. 2026-30; § 132-6.2 last amended S.L. 2004-129 — no 2024, 2025 or 2026 amendment; no pending 2026 modification listed for §§ 132-6, 132-6.2, 132-1.4A(l), 132-10)
verified.notes: No statewide per-page figure for municipalities; the city sets its B&W rate under the actual-cost ceiling (NC-0019) as defined in § 132-6.2(b) (NC-9001) and the § 132-1(b) 'free or at minimal cost' policy (NC-9002). Agency regime note: the Governor's July 2018 guidance for Cabinet agencies recommends five cents per page for printed copies (NC-9010) — state-agency guidance only, not binding on cities. Ch. 132 binds 'every public office ... of any county, unit, special district or other political subdivision' (§ 132-1(a)).

NE.snippet: A custodian may charge a fee for providing copies, but the fee shall not exceed the actual added cost of making the copies available.

verified.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by statute, the public body, public entity, or public official which is the custodian of a public record may charge a fee for providing copies of such public record pursuant to subdivision (1)(b) of this section, which fee shall not exceed the actual added cost of making the copies available. For purposes of this subdivision, (i) for photocopies, the actual added cost of making the copies available shall not exceed the amount of the reasonably calculated actual added cost of the photocopies, which may include a reasonably apportioned cost of the supplies, such as paper, toner, and equipment, used in preparing the copies, as well as any additional payment obligation of the custodian for time of contractors necessarily incurred to comply with the request for copies,
verified.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
verified.notes: Standard is 'actual added cost of making the copies available'; for photocopies the components are enumerated (reasonably apportioned supplies such as paper, toner, equipment; contractor time). No statewide per-page rate binds municipalities. Official guidance (Attorney General Outline, Rev. 7/2024): the AG's enforcement policy 'will not question copying charges of up to 25 cents per page' in addition to other allowable charges — an enforcement safe harbor, not a legal cap; recorded as NE-9001. Applies to every 'public body, public entity, or public official which is the custodian' (state, county, city, village, political subdivision per § 84-712.01(1)).

verified.unit: USD per page (letter size or smaller | legal size or larger)
verified.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(b)(1), as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2
verified.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law or regulation and except as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection, the fee assessed for the duplication of a government record embodied in the form of printed matter shall be $0.05 per letter size page or smaller, and $0.07 per legal size page or larger.
verified.effective_status: Current (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5 last amended P.L.2024, c.16, s.2, effective 2024-09-03; official codified text checked 2026-08-18 shows no later amendment)
verified.notes: Mandatory flat rate ('shall be'), not a ceiling. P.L.2024, c.16 DELETED the former sentence permitting an agency to charge a demonstrated higher actual duplication cost, so no municipal ordinance or actual-cost calculation may raise the rate (GRC Handbook 8th ed.: 'P.L. 2024, c.16 removed consideration of calculating an actual cost exceeding the foregoing copying costs'). Exceptions: fees 'otherwise provided by law or regulation' for specific record types (e.g., N.J.S.A. 39:4-131 accident reports add up to $5 for non-in-person requests); GRC FAQ: municipal ordinances do not qualify as such law/regulation. Applies to every 'public agency', which by N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.1 includes political subdivisions (municipalities).

NV.snippet: A governmental entity may charge a fee for a copy, but the fee must not exceed the actual cost to provide the copy unless a specific statute or regulation sets the fee.

verified.unit: USD per page (city sets under actual-cost ceiling)
verified.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, a governmental entity may charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record. Such a fee must not exceed the actual cost to the governmental entity to provide the copy of the public record unless a specific statute or regulation sets a fee that the governmental entity must charge for the copy. A governmental entity shall not charge a fee for providing a copy of a public record if a specific statute or regulation requires the governmental entity to provide the copy without charge. | “Actual cost” means the direct cost incurred by a governmental entity in the provision of a public record, including, without limitation, the cost of ink, toner, paper, media and postage. The term does not include a cost that a governmental entity incurs regardless of whether or not a person requests a copy of a particular public record.
verified.effective_status: Current (NRS 239.052 last amended 2013; NRS 239.005(1) amended 2019 SB 287)
verified.notes: No statewide per-page figure for municipalities. 'Governmental entity' expressly includes officers and units of a political subdivision (NRS 239.005(5)), so the actual-cost ceiling binds cities. Prior status said 'delegated to regulation'; NRS 239.052(1)'s 'unless a specific statute or regulation sets a fee' is an override clause, not a delegation to a municipal fee instrument - no such general instrument exists. NRS 239.052(3) (NV-9006) requires each entity to prepare/maintain and post its own fee list. Direct costs are ink, toner, paper, media, postage. AB 51 (2025), which would have allowed a 'reasonable fee for the use of its personnel or technological resources', died in committee 2025-04-12.

NY.snippet: Fees for paper copies shall not exceed 25 cents per photocopy not exceeding 9 by 14 inches, unless a different fee is prescribed by statute.

OH.snippet: Copies of public records shall be made available 'at cost' — the office may not charge more than its actual cost of making the copy.

verified.source_authority: Ohio Rev. Code § 149.43(B)(1); State ex rel. Warren Newspapers v. Hutson, 1994-Ohio-5, ¶ 25-26; AG Model Public Records Policy
verified.source_language: Subject to division (B)(8) of this section, upon request by any person, a public office or person responsible for public records shall make copies of the requested public record available to the requester at cost and within a reasonable period of time.
verified.effective_status: Current (R.C. 149.43 as amended eff. Sept. 30, 2025, H.B. 96, 136th G.A.; a further amendment by H.B. 31, 136th G.A., eff. Sept. 7, 2026, is enacted-awaiting-effect and does not touch the fee/payment language)
verified.notes: Standard = 'at cost' = 'actual cost' (Hutson). No statewide per-page figure for municipalities; the city sets its per-page value by policy under the actual-cost ceiling (AG model policy: '[X] cents per page'). Actual cost excludes employee labor (OH-9002); Bonnell (cited in Hutson) describes cost components as toner, paper and copying time. Applies to every 'public office' (state, county, city, village, township, school district — R.C. 149.43(A)(1)); Ohio runs one regime for all public bodies and has no separate state-agency fee schedule.

OK.snippet: The record copying fee may not exceed twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for records 8.5 by 14 inches or smaller.

OR.snippet: A public body may establish fees reasonably calculated to reimburse it for its actual cost of making public records available, including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the records in organization or media

citations: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)
PA.snippet: Under the OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule, an agency may charge up to $0.25 per copy for black-and-white photocopies (8.5x11 or 8.5x14), reduced to $0.20 per copy beyond the first 1,000 copies.

verified.unit: USD per copy (copies 1–1,000 | copies beyond 1,000); a 'copy' is one side of a sheet of 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 paper
verified.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
verified.source_language: Black & White Copies (first 1,000) — Up to $0.25 per copy. Black & White Copies (beyond 1,000) — Up to $0.20 per copy. A "copy" is either a single-sided copy, or one side of a double-sided copy, on 8.5"x11" or 8.5"x14" paper.
verified.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review

'Up to' = ceiling; the city sets its rate under it. Existing PA-0040 misdated the schedule and paraphrased — amended by PA-9001. Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

SC.snippet: Fees for copies may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies.

verified.value: prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies
verified.unit: USD per page (city sets under the standard)
verified.source_language: Fees charged by a public body must be uniform for copies of the same record or document and may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies. The public body shall develop a fee schedule to be posted online.
verified.effective_status: Current (2017 Act No. 67, eff. May 19, 2017; no later amendment through 2025 session; no 2026 act found)
verified.notes: No cents-per-page figure anywhere in SC law; the copy fee is bounded by a non-numeric ceiling ('prevailing commercial rate') and must be uniform for the same record and posted in the body's online fee schedule (city sets the number). 'Public body' expressly includes municipalities (§ 30-4-20(a)). Guidance only, not binding on cities: the AG's own-office schedule charges $0.20/page; the 2020 SC OIG survey benchmarked commercial self-service B&W copies at $0.08–$0.14 (Apr. 2019). Existing row SC-0009 records the same clause with constraint_basis=ceiling — a non-numeric ceiling; treated here as actual_cost_standard because no number can be extracted.

TN.snippet: For each standard 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 black-and-white copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per-page charge of up to 15 cents ($0.15).

verified.unit: USD per page (standard 8.5x11 / 8.5x14 B&W; duplex = 2 pages)
verified.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.A (delegated from Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)(i) via § 8-4-604(a)(1)(A))
verified.source_language: For each standard 8½” x 11” or 8½” x 14” copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per page charge of up to 15 cents ($0.15) for black and white copies and up to 50 cents ($0.50) for color copies. If producing duplex (front and back) copies, a charge for two separate pages may be imposed for each single duplex copy.
verified.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017 (submitted to ACOG Nov. 8, 2016). Verified still posted as the operative schedule on the OORC Policies, Guidelines & Forms page as of 2026-08-19; no revision published despite § 8-4-604(a)(1)(B) 'revised at least annually'.
verified.notes: 'up to' = ceiling under a Permission; city sets the operative rate at or below $0.15 in its adopted policy; may go above only with documented actual-cost analysis (§ II.C, TN-0031). Delegation followed: statute → § 8-4-604 → Schedule (opened). OORC Schedule figures bind every 'records custodian'/'governmental entity' subject to the TPRA (state, county and municipal); the schedule is a guideline a custodian 'may use' (§ 8-4-604(a)(1)(A)) and charges must be adopted in the local policy (§ 10-7-503(g)(1)(C)); exceeding the schedule requires documented actual cost (Schedule § II.C) and forfeits the safe-harbor presumption.

TX.snippet: The copy charge must be an amount that reasonably includes all costs related to reproducing the information, including materials, labor, and overhead.

verified.unit: USD per page or part of a page, each recorded side a page (AG-established rate | municipal ceiling absent AG exemption = AG rate + 25%)
verified.source_authority: 1 Tex. Admin. Code § 70.3(b)(1); Tex. Gov't Code § 552.262(a)
verified.source_language: (1) Standard paper copy. The charge for standard paper copies reproduced by means of an office machine copier or a computer printer is $.10 per page or part of a page. Each side that has recorded information is considered a page. [§ 552.262(a):] The charges for providing copies of public information may not be excessive and may not exceed the actual cost of producing the information or for making public information that exists in a paper record available for inspection. A governmental body, other than an agency of state government, may determine its own charges for providing copies of public information and its own charge, deposit, or bond for making public information that exists in a paper record available for inspection but may not charge an amount that is greater than 25 percent more than the amount established by the attorney general unless the governmental body requests an exemption under Subsection (c).
verified.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.3 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
verified.notes: Delegation followed: § 552.262 → 1 TAC § 70.3(b)(1) opened on the SOS TAC portal (last amended eff. Feb. 22, 2007). Municipal regime: § 552.262(a) lets a governmental body other than a state agency set its own charge up to 25 percent above the AG-established amount without an exemption (1 TAC § 70.1(b)(2), § 70.4(c)); state agencies must use the AG amount. Charges may never exceed actual cost. Cities holding an AG exemption (published annually in the Texas Register) may differ. $0.125 is arithmetic (0.10 × 1.25), not a printed figure. For 50-or-fewer-page paper requests the per-page charge is the ONLY charge (TX-0026).

verified.unit: USD per page (city sets by ordinance/policy under the actual-cost standard)
verified.source_language: (1)(a) Subject to Subsection (5), a governmental entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover the governmental entity's actual cost of providing a record. (b) A fee under Subsection (1)(a) shall be approved by the governmental entity's executive officer. | (3)(c) Political subdivisions shall establish fees by ordinance or written formal policy adopted by the governing body. | (3) Each ordinance or policy relating to information practices shall: ... (c) provide guidelines for establishment of fees in accordance with Section 63G-2-203; ... | (2)(c) If any political subdivision does not adopt and maintain an ordinance or policy, then that political subdivision is subject to this chapter.

verified.notes: Utah sets no per-page or per-item figure for any public body. The state's binding constraint is the § 63G-2-203(1)(a) 'reasonable fee to cover ... actual cost' standard; the operative figure is set by the political subdivision by ordinance or written formal policy adopted by the governing body (§ 63G-2-203(3)(c)), and a political subdivision's GRAMA ordinance/policy must 'provide guidelines for establishment of fees in accordance with Section 63G-2-203' (§ 63G-2-701(3)(c)). Archives official form (2025): 'Additional fees are established by a local ordinance or policy'. State-agency fees are set through the budget process / § 63J-1-504 (§ 63G-2-203(3)(b)) — agency schedules (e.g., the annual State Agency Fees authorization acts, the AG office GRAMA fee schedule) do not bind municipalities.

verified.source_language: The public officer may require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before the requester may receive any public records. If the public officer elects to charge a fee, the public officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment. The requester may opt not to pay the fee and thus not receive any substantive response. Additionally, the public officer shall have the discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records.

IN.snippet: The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of ten cents ($0.10) per non-color page or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per color page, or the agency's actual cost.

verified.unit: USD per page (color), or the agency's actual cost of copying if greater (paper + per-page equipment cost only)
verified.source_language: This subsection applies to a public agency that is not a state agency. The fiscal body (as defined in IC 36-1-2-6) of the public agency, or the governing body, if there is no fiscal body, shall establish a fee schedule for the certification or copying of documents. The fee for certification of documents may not exceed five dollars ($5) per document. The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of: (1) ten cents ($0.10) per page for copies that are not color copies or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for color copies; or (2) the actual cost to the agency of copying the document. As used in this subsection, "actual cost" means the cost of paper and the per-page cost for use of copying or facsimile equipment and does not include labor costs or overhead costs. A fee established under this subsection must be uniform throughout the public agency and uniform to all purchasers.

If the public officer elects to charge a fee, the public officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment. The requester may opt not to pay the fee and thus not receive any substantive response. Additionally, the public officer shall have the discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records. | § 36-21-213(b): A custodial law enforcement agency may charge a reasonable fee for redaction and editing of a recording.

CO.snippet: For a copy, printout, or photograph in a format other than a standard page, the custodian may charge a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing it.

verified.value: actual cost of providing the copy, printout, or photograph (other format); data-manipulation fee 'reasonable' and not to exceed actual cost
verified.source_language: A custodian may charge a fee not to exceed twenty-five cents per standard page for a copy of a public record or a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing a copy, printout, or photograph of a public record in a format other than a standard page; except that a custodian shall not charge a per-page fee for providing records in a digital or electronic format. || If, in response to a specific request, the state or any of its agencies, institutions, or political subdivisions has performed a manipulation of data so as to generate a record in a form not used by the state or by said agency, institution, or political subdivision, a reasonable fee may be charged to the person making the request. Such fee shall not exceed the actual cost of manipulating the said data and generating the said record in accordance with the request. Persons making subsequent requests for the same or similar records may be charged a fee not in excess of the original fee.
verified.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)

verified.effective_status: Current — Gen. Stat. rev. to Jan. 1, 2025; § 1-212 not in the 2026 Supplement (rev. to Jan. 1, 2026 — only § 1-210(b)(17) amended in 2025); last amended P.A. 12-205; 2026-session public acts (through P.A. 26-68) searched — none amend § 1-212

verified.source_language: Such copies may be obtained in any form designated by the requester in which the public record is maintained or produced, including, but not limited to, printouts, electronic data, discs, tapes, and photocopies. | For purposes of this subdivision, (i) for photocopies, the actual added cost of making the copies available shall not exceed the amount of the reasonably calculated actual added cost of the photocopies, which may include a reasonably apportioned cost of the supplies, such as paper, toner, and equipment, used in preparing the copies, as well as any additional payment obligation of the custodian for time of contractors necessarily incurred to comply with the request for copies, (ii) for printouts of computerized data on paper, the actual added cost of making the copies available shall include the reasonably calculated actual added cost of computer run time and the cost of materials for making the copy, and (iii) for electronic data, the actual added cost of making the copies available shall include the reasonably calculated actual added cost of the computer run time, any necessary analysis and programming by the public body, public entity, public official, or third-party information technology services company contracted to provide computer services to the public body, public entity, or public official, and the production of the report in the form furnished to the requester.

verified.value: actual direct cost of providing the copy or copies (special service charge), reasonable
verified.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(c) and (d), as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2
verified.source_language: Whenever the nature, format, manner of collation, or volume of a government record embodied in the form of printed matter to be inspected, examined, or copied pursuant to this section is such that the record cannot be reproduced by ordinary document copying equipment in ordinary business size or involves an extraordinary expenditure of time and effort to accommodate the request, the public agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplicating the record, a special service charge that shall be based upon the actual direct cost of providing the copy or copies, and such special service charge shall be reasonable. The custodian shall provide the requestor with an explanation for and an itemized list of the fees or charges. The requestor shall have the opportunity to review and object to any fee or charge prior to it being incurred. There shall be a rebuttable presumption that the fees or charges presented by the custodian are reasonable. If the requestor objects to the fees or charges, the burden of proof shall be on the requestor to demonstrate that the fees or charges are unreasonable.

verified.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.C, § III.E
verified.source_language: If a governmental entity's actual costs are higher than those reflected above, or if the requested records are produced on a medium other than 8½” x 11” or 8½” x 14” paper, the governmental entity may develop its own charges. The governmental entity must establish a schedule of charges documenting “actual cost” and state the calculation and reasoning for its charges in a properly adopted policy. A governmental entity may charge less than those charges reflected above. Charges greater than 15 cents ($0.15) for black and white copies and 50 cents ($0.50) for color copies can be assessed or collected only when there is documented analysis of the fact that the higher charges represent the governmental entity's actual cost of producing such material, unless there exists another basis in law for such charges. ... E. If it is not practicable or feasible for the records custodian to produce copies internally, the records custodian may use an outside vendor and charge the costs to the requester.
verified.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017 (submitted to ACOG Nov. 8, 2016). Verified still posted as the operative schedule on the OORC Policies, Guidelines & Forms page as of 2026-08-19; no revision published despite § 8-4-604(a)(1)(B) 'revised at least annually'.
verified.notes: Photos, maps, transcripts, etc. fall under 'medium other than 8½ x 11 or 8½ x 14 paper' → entity's own documented actual-cost charge; vendor cost pass-through when internal production is not practicable. Commercial-value GIS maps have a separate statutory regime (§ 10-7-506(c), see 'commercial').

verified.unit: USD or actual cost per item (city sets by ordinance/policy under the actual-cost standard)
verified.source_language: (1)(a) Subject to Subsection (5), a governmental entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover the governmental entity's actual cost of providing a record. (b) A fee under Subsection (1)(a) shall be approved by the governmental entity's executive officer. | (2)(a) When a governmental entity compiles a record in a form other than that normally maintained by the governmental entity, the actual costs under this section may include the following: (i) the cost of staff time for compiling, formatting, manipulating, packaging, summarizing, or tailoring the record either into an organization or media to meet the person's request; (ii) the cost of staff time for search, retrieval, and other direct administrative costs for complying with a request; and (iii) in the case of fees for a record that is the result of computer output other than word processing, the actual incremental cost of providing the electronic services and products together with a reasonable portion of the costs associated with formatting or interfacing the information for particular users, and the administrative costs as set forth in Subsections (2)(a)(i) and (ii). | (8)(c) A governmental entity may require a person who makes a request under Subsection (8)(a) to pay the governmental entity, in accordance with Section 63G-2-203, for providing the information or record as requested.
verified.effective_status: Current (63G-2-203 last amended Ch. 33 (S.B. 188), 2025 General Session, effective 3/17/2025 — technical wording change to (8)(a)(ii) only; no 2026 General Session amendment as of 2026-08-19)
verified.notes: No specialty-reproduction figure. Where the entity compiles/formats a record into a form or medium not normally maintained (which is what a photo print, map plot or transcript usually is), § 63G-2-203(2)(a) lists the actual-cost components that may be included and § 63G-2-201(8)(c) authorizes charging for the tailored product 'in accordance with Section 63G-2-203'. Figure set locally by ordinance/policy. Utah sets no per-page or per-item figure for any public body. The state's binding constraint is the § 63G-2-203(1)(a) 'reasonable fee to cover ... actual cost' standard; the operative figure is set by the political subdivision by ordinance or written formal policy adopted by the governing body (§ 63G-2-203(3)(c)), and a political subdivision's GRAMA ordinance/policy must 'provide guidelines for establishment of fees in accordance with Section 63G-2-203' (§ 63G-2-701(3)(c)). Archives official form (2025): 'Additional fees are established by a local ordinance or policy'. State-agency fees are set through the budget process / § 63J-1-504 (§ 63G-2-203(3)(b)) — agency schedules (e.g., the annual State Agency Fees authorization acts, the AG office GRAMA fee schedule) do not bind municipalities.

IN.snippet: The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of ten cents ($0.10) per non-color page or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per color page, or the agency's actual cost.

verified.source_language: This subsection applies to a public agency that is not a state agency. The fiscal body (as defined in IC 36-1-2-6) of the public agency, or the governing body, if there is no fiscal body, shall establish a fee schedule for the certification or copying of documents. The fee for certification of documents may not exceed five dollars ($5) per document. The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of: (1) ten cents ($0.10) per page for copies that are not color copies or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for color copies; or (2) the actual cost to the agency of copying the document. As used in this subsection, "actual cost" means the cost of paper and the per-page cost for use of copying or facsimile equipment and does not include labor costs or overhead costs. A fee established under this subsection must be uniform throughout the public agency and uniform to all purchasers.

verified.effective_status: Current (R.C. 149.43 as amended eff. Sept. 30, 2025, H.B. 96, 136th G.A.; a further amendment by H.B. 31, 136th G.A., eff. Sept. 7, 2026, is enacted-awaiting-effect and does not touch the fee/payment language)
verified.notes: No graduated/volume page bands anywhere in R.C. 149.43, the AG manual or model policy. Any banding a city adopts must still reflect actual cost per copy. Searched: R.C. 149.43 (all versions Oct. 24, 2024 through Sept. 7, 2026 on codes.ohio.gov, including the H.B. 315 (Apr. 9, 2025), H.B. 96 (Sept. 30, 2025) and H.B. 31 (Sept. 7, 2026) versions); R.C. 149.011, 109.43; the AG's 2026 Sunshine Laws Manual (fees ch. 2 §§ 11-13, policy ch. 7); the AG Model Public Records Policy; the AG index 'Opinions Interpreting Ohio's Sunshine Laws' (fee-related: 89-073, 99-012, 2001-012, 2014-009, 2022-018); State ex rel. Warren Newspapers v. Hutson (1994). Ohio has no administrative-code fee schedule for public records and no uniform state schedule; no municipal figure exists beyond 'at cost'.

OK.snippet: The record copying fee may not exceed twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for records 8.5 by 14 inches or smaller.

citations: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)
PA.snippet: Under the OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule, an agency may charge up to $0.25 per copy for black-and-white photocopies (8.5x11 or 8.5x14), reduced to $0.20 per copy beyond the first 1,000 copies.

verified.unit: USD per copy, black-and-white only (color has no tier); tier counted per request in copies
verified.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024 per OOR web page), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)(1)(i)
verified.source_language: Black & White Copies (first 1,000) — Up to $0.25 per copy. Black & White Copies (beyond 1,000) — Up to $0.20 per copy.
verified.effective_status: Current — OOR web page states the schedule was adopted Dec. 30, 2024 (the linked PDF's header reads 'Updated December 30, 2022'; content identical); RTKL requires biannual OOR review
verified.notes: Two-band schedule; both bands are ceilings. Binds Commonwealth agencies and local agencies (municipalities are 'local agencies'); judicial and legislative agencies set their own duplication fees under § 1307(b)(1)(ii)-(iii).

SC.snippet: Fees for copies may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies.

verified.source_language: Fees charged by a public body must be uniform for copies of the same record or document and may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies.
verified.effective_status: Current (2017 Act No. 67, eff. May 19, 2017; no later amendment through 2025 session; no 2026 act found)
verified.notes: No graduated/volume page bands in SC law. Searched: S.C. Code Title 30 ch. 4 (FOIA, all sections; fee content confined to § 30-4-30(B)-(C)); S.C. Code of Regulations index and ch. 12 (Archives & History) — no FOIA fee regulation exists; SC Attorney General FOIA page and opinion search (scag.gov/search: 'FOIA fee 30-4-30', 'prorated hourly salary', 'prevailing commercial rate', 'FOIA redaction fee') — opened AG Ops. of June 28, 2019 (Forrest/Hudson), Jan. 24, 2020 (McCurdy, clerks of court), May 31, 2024 (Swindler, BWC); 2024, 2025 and 2026 Acts lists on scstatehouse.gov (no FOIA fee act); S. 6 (2025-2026) which re-states § 30-4-30(B) unchanged and remains in Senate Judiciary. The only constraint touching tiers is uniformity ('must be uniform for copies of the same record or document') — a per-requester non-discrimination rule; whether volume bands are consistent with it is not addressed by any official source (not opined here).

citations: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.A
TN.snippet: For each standard 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 black-and-white copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per-page charge of up to 15 cents ($0.15).

verified.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II (searched); OORC Model Public Records Policy § VI.D; Tenn. Code Ann. §§ 10-7-503, 8-4-604
verified.source_language: For each standard 8½” x 11” or 8½” x 14” copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per page charge of up to 15 cents ($0.15) for black and white copies and up to 50 cents ($0.50) for color copies. If producing duplex (front and back) copies, a charge for two separate pages may be imposed for each single duplex copy.
verified.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017 (submitted to ACOG Nov. 8, 2016). Verified still posted as the operative schedule on the OORC Policies, Guidelines & Forms page as of 2026-08-19; no revision published despite § 8-4-604(a)(1)(B) 'revised at least annually'.
verified.notes: Documented absence: the schedule states a single flat per-page ceiling for each of B&W and color with no volume bands; the only page-count rule is that a duplex sheet may be charged as two pages. Searched: Schedule §§ II–III, Model Policy § VI, Best Practices § III, § 8-4-604(a)(1)(A) (which lists population size/complexity as factors the OORC was to consider — the resulting schedule did not band by volume), OORC FAQ.

TX.snippet: The copy charge must be an amount that reasonably includes all costs related to reproducing the information, including materials, labor, and overhead.

verified.source_authority: 1 Tex. Admin. Code § 70.3(b)(1); Tex. Gov't Code § 552.261(a)
verified.source_language: The charge for standard paper copies reproduced by means of an office machine copier or a computer printer is $.10 per page or part of a page.
verified.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.3 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
verified.notes: Coverage: Gov't Code ch. 552 subch. F, 1 TAC ch. 70 (§§ 70.1-70.13), 2026 PIA Handbook Part VII. No volume-graduated per-page bands exist; the per-page rate is flat. The only volume threshold (50 pages of paper records) switches labor/overhead on, not the per-page rate — see labor.billableWhen. Nothing bars a city from adopting bands under its § 552.262(a) discretion so long as each rate stays within the 25% variance and actual cost.

UT.snippet: An entity may not charge a fee for the first quarter hour of staff time spent responding to a request.

verified.source_language: (coverage note — no graduated per-page band provision exists in Utah Code § 63G-2-203 or elsewhere in GRAMA)
verified.effective_status: Current (63G-2-203 last amended Ch. 33 (S.B. 188), 2025 General Session, effective 3/17/2025 — technical wording change to (8)(a)(ii) only; no 2026 General Session amendment as of 2026-08-19)
verified.notes: No graduated page bands anywhere in GRAMA. The only volume-linked provisions are non-fee: § 63G-2-201(10) lets an entity require a requester of >50 pages to make the copies (and waive copy fees) and § 63G-2-204(6)(c) treats voluminous requests as an 'extraordinary circumstance' for the response clock. Searched: Utah Code § 63G-2-203 (all subsections, current text as amended 2025), §§ 63G-2-201, -204, -209, -401, -701; Utah Municipal Code § 10-8-85.6; 2024–2026 General Session passed-bill lists (records/fee bills); Utah Division of Archives and Records Service GRAMA FAQ, guidelines page, and official forms (GRAMA Request Form; GRAMA Request for Payment or Prepayment 2025); Government Records Office decision 2024-202. No Utah Administrative Code rule sets GRAMA fees for political subdivisions; the AG issues no GRAMA fee opinions/schedule binding cities.

WA.snippet: Absent a published actual-cost calculation, the agency may charge up to fifteen cents per page for photocopies or printed copies of electronic records.

WI.snippet: An authority may impose a fee for a copy of a record not exceeding the actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction and transcription, unless a fee is otherwise specifically established or authorized by law.

verified.source_language: No provision. Coverage: Searched: Ala. verified.notes: No free-page allowance in state law for any public body; § 36-12-44(h) preserves the officer's freedom to process 'in a manner that is less expensive' (AL-9009), so a city may adopt one. Official link is the Legislature's Code of Alabama viewer (browse Title 36 > Chapter 12 > Article 3; section text also served by its GraphQL endpoint https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql, query codeOfAlabamaSection); alternate direct text: enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF.

verified.source_language: The custodian of such records shall promptly furnish such copies, printouts or photographs and may charge a fee if the facilities are available, except that public records for purposes listed in section 39-122 or 39-127 shall be furnished without charge.
verified.effective_status: Amended effective September 26, 2025 (Laws 2025, ch. 102, SB 1372, approved May 2, 2025; general effective date of the 57th Leg., 1st Reg. Sess.) — codified text opened at azleg.gov 2026-08-19
verified.notes: No free-page allowance. Arizona's only statutory no-charge rules are purpose/requester-based (claims against the United States, § 39-122; crime victims' police report/audio/video, § 39-127), not volume-based. Searched: A.R.S. Title 39, ch. 1, art. 2 (§§ 39-121 to 39-129, incl. § 39-171) opened at azleg.gov 2026-08-19; A.R.S. § 39-121.03 (commercial); Ariz. Att'y Gen. Op. Arizona has no administrative code provisions on municipal public-records fees (no rulemaking delegation in § 39-121.01) — nothing found on this item.

CA.snippet: For ordinary production of electronic records, an agency may not charge for the ancillary staff time of searching for and redacting/reviewing records; such time is chargeable only within the narrow data-extraction cost-s

verified.source_language: A requester who inspects a disclosable record on the premises of the agency has the right to use the requester’s equipment on those premises, without being charged any fees or costs, to photograph or otherwise copy or reproduce the record in a manner that does not require the equipment to make physical contact with the record, unless the means of copy or reproduction would result in either of the following: (1) Damage to the record. (2) Unauthorized access to the agency’s computer systems or secured networks by using software, equipment, or any other technology capable of accessing, altering, or compromising the agency’s electronic records.
verified.effective_status: Current (added Stats. 2021, ch. 614 (AB 473), operative Jan. 1, 2023; no amendment 2024–2026 as of 2026-08-19)
verified.notes: No free-page allowance. CO.snippet: The custodian shall not impose any charge for the first hour of time expended in research and retrieval of public records.

verified.source_language: A custodian may charge a fee not to exceed twenty-five cents per standard page for a copy of a public record or a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing a copy, printout, or photograph of a public record in a format other than a standard page; except that a custodian shall not charge a per-page fee for providing records in a digital or electronic format.
verified.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)

AG Formal Opinion No. 01-1 (2001). Colorado has no administrative-code CORA fee schedule binding local bodies.

verified.source_authority: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-212 (searched); FOIC FIC 2018-0293 (Stedman) as quoted in FIC 2025-0213 ¶¶ 59-61

GA.snippet: No labor charge may be made for the first quarter hour of search, retrieval, or redaction.

verified.source_language: In addition to a charge for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records, an agency may charge a fee for the copying of records or data, not to exceed 10¢ per page for letter or legal size documents or, in the case of other documents, the actual cost of producing the copy.

ID.snippet: No fee shall be charged for the first two (2) hours of labor in responding to a resident's public records request.

verified.source_language: Except for fees that are authorized or prescribed under other provisions of Idaho law, no fee shall be charged for the first two (2) hours of labor in responding to a request submitted by a resident for public records, or for copying the first one hundred (100) pages of paper records that are requested by a resident.
verified.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
verified.notes: Resident-only ('a request submitted by a resident'; resident defined § 74-101(15): 30-day continuous Idaho domicile, incl. domestic entities). Nonresidents get no free allotment (§ 74-102(10)(g), ID-9001). Carve-out: fees 'authorized or prescribed under other provisions of Idaho law' (e.g. recorder/court fees) are not displaced (ID-9013). Applies to 'public agency' = state and local agencies.

verified.source_language: But the term “extraction” does not cover every process that might be colloquially described as “taking information out.” It does not, for example, cover time spent searching for responsive records in an e-mail inbox or a computer’s documents folder. Nor, for similar reasons, does “extraction” cover the cost of redacting exempt data from otherwise producible electronic records.

The director of research shall post the adjusted maximum hourly fee on the website of the general assembly. || Section 24-72-205 (6) (b), C.R.S., requires the Director of Research of the Legislative Council Staff to adjust the Colorado Open Records Act maximum hourly fee for the research and retrieval of public documents for inflation on July 1, 2019, and each five years thereafter. The maximum hourly fee increased from $30.00 to $33.58 on July 1, 2019. Effective July 1, 2024, the maximum hourly fee will increase to $41.37. Before increasing the fee, government entities must revise and publish their Colorado Open Records Act policies to include the new fee.

verified.source_language: (1) An amount equal to the hourly salary attributed to all agency employees engaged in providing the requested computer-stored public record, including their time performing the formatting or programming functions necessary to provide the copy as requested, but not including search or retrieval costs except as provided in subdivision (4) of this subsection; || FOIC FIC 2025-0213: 35. The provisions of §1-212, G.S., set forth all permissible fees that an agency may charge in connection with providing copies of public records. See §1-212(a), G.S., ("[t]he fee for any copy provided in accordance with the [FOI] Act.") (Emphasis added); see also §1-212(b), G.S., ("[t]he fee for any copy provided in accordance with subsection (a) of section 1-211. . . .") (Emphasis added). 36. In the context of non-computer-stored records (i.e. paper records), the explicit terms of §§1-212(a)(A) and (B), G.S., limit permissible fees to copying fees of twenty-five cents per page for state agencies and fifty cents per page for all other public agencies. 37. It is clear, therefore, that the fees a public agency may charge for paper records are solely derived from the costs attributable to providing the records in the prescribed medium. As an agency would not be able to provide original versions of paper records to requestors, they must make physical copies of such records to provide them to requestors. In the case of paper records, the physical copy is the prescribed medium in which the agency is obligated to provide records. Notably, nothing in §1-212(a), G.S., would permit the respondents to charge a fee for (or predicate their fee estimate on) any of the labor costs identified in paragraph 33, above.

verified.source_language: Fees for requests made by residents shall not exceed reasonable labor costs necessarily incurred in responding to a public records request, and if charged, shall reflect the personnel and quantity of time that are reasonably necessary to process a request. Fees for requests made by residents for labor costs shall be charged at the per hour pay rate of the lowest paid administrative staff employee or public official of the public agency who is necessary and qualified to process the request. If a request from a resident requires redactions to be made by an attorney who is employed by the public agency, the rate charged shall be no more than the per hour rate of the lowest paid attorney within the public agency who is necessary and qualified to process the public records request. If a request from a resident is submitted to a public agency that does not have an attorney on staff, and requires redactions by an attorney, the rate shall be no more than the usual and customary rate of the attorney who is retained by the public agency for that purpose. | Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, a public agency or public official may charge fees for labor and copying costs associated with locating and copying documents requested by a person who is not a resident or an employee of a resident. The fee rates and schedule for requests made by persons who are not residents or employees of residents shall be at the discretion of the public agency or public official as long as such fees do not exceed actual costs of the public agency or public official.

July 1, 2026); (ii) 'direct cost' (105% of labor to retrieve electronically stored data + medium) for electronic duplicates under § 8(g) and reprogramming under § 6(c) (IN-9005, IN-9006, IN-0012); (iii) school corporations/charter schools only: search time beyond 5 hours at ≤ lesser of the searcher's hourly rate or $20/hour (§ 8(m), IN-9015 — not municipal).

KS.snippet: Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs not attributable to furnishing the requested records.

verified.source_language: In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records. … If the public agency incurs costs for staff time to provide access to or furnish copies of public records, the agency shall use in good faith the lowest-cost category of staff reasonably necessary to provide access to or furnish copies of public records. Charges for staff time shall be based on the employee's salary or hourly wage. Charges for staff time shall not include the costs of employee benefits.
verified.effective_status: Amended effective 2025-07-01 (L. 2025, ch. 89, § 1 [HB 2134]); no 2026 amendment

Search/retrieval staff time is chargeable as part of 'the cost of staff time required to make the information available'; the rate is capped at 'the employee's salary or hourly wage', excluding benefits, and the agency must use in good faith 'the lowest-cost category of staff reasonably necessary'. City supplies actual wage-based rates. Agency-specific published rates (DoA attorney $60/clerical $18/IT $38; SOS clerical $21/attorney $52/IT $42) are those agencies' own wage-based figures, not municipal values.

LA.snippet: When examination is conducted outside regular working hours, persons representing the custodian are entitled to reasonable compensation, paid by the public body and funded in advance by the party demanding the extraordin

verified.source_language: No provision of the Public Records Law directly authorizes such a charge to the requester. We must therefore return to La. R.S. 44:32(C)(3) and the default rule that a requester may not be charged a fee in connection with a request to examine public records, nor for a custodian's pre-examination retrieval, review, and separation of records. See La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 15-0173, supra. We are therefore of the opinion that a custodian may require a requester to provide advance payment of an employee's compensation only for the time the employee is present during the requester's examination, not for pre-examination preparation, absent a judicial declaration allowing otherwise.
verified.effective_status: Current (opinion not withdrawn; statute text unchanged on this point through Acts 2024, No. 411)
verified.notes: Louisiana authorizes only 'reasonable fees for making copies' for local custodians; the AG's 'default rule' is that a requester may not be charged for 'a custodian's pre-examination retrieval, review, and separation of records' absent judicial authorization, and DOJ's 2023 guidance states 'Can't charge for the time to process the request' (LA-9012). Hence a search/retrieval hourly rate is not a lawful municipal parameter. Sole labor-like charge in the statute is 'reasonable compensation' for the custodian's representative during after-hours examination, funded in advance (LA-9007) — that is supervision of inspection, not search.

verified.value: the actual cost incurred for such extensive use of information technology resources or the labor costs of the personnel providing the services (charge 'shall be reasonable'); ordinary search/copying labor is not chargeable because 'actual cost' excludes costs the agency would have incurred if the request had not been made
verified.unit: USD per hour (soft standard: actual labor cost of the personnel providing the services; chargeable only when the request requires 'extensive' clerical/supervisory assistance or IT use)
verified.source_authority: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 132-6.2(b); N.C. Attorney General, Open Government Guide (2019) p. 20
verified.source_language: Notwithstanding the provisions of this subsection, if the request is such as to require extensive use of information technology resources or extensive clerical or supervisory assistance by personnel of the agency involved, or if producing the record in the medium requested results in a greater use of information technology resources than that established by the agency for reproduction of the volume of information requested, then the agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplication, a special service charge, which shall be reasonable and shall be based on the actual cost incurred for such extensive use of information technology resources or the labor costs of the personnel providing the services, or for a greater use of information technology resources that is actually incurred by the agency or attributable to the agency. || "Actual cost" is defined as "direct, chargeable costs related to the reproduction of a public record as determined by generally accepted accounting principles." The law does not give examples of actual costs but it does say that actual cost may not include costs the agency would have incurred if the copy request had not been made. This means that under most circumstances, fees may not include the labor costs of the agency employees who make the copies. However, if making the copies involves extensive clerical or supervisory assistance, the agency may charge a special service fee in addition to actual duplication costs. This service charge must be reasonable and based on actual labor costs but cannot be charged to recover fees for time spent examining or removing confidential information from records. Agencies also may charge to recover the costs of mailing copies. Complaints or disputes about all records copying fees may be directed to the State Chief Information Officer or their designee for mediation.

A special service charge reflecting the calculated labor cost may be included in the fee for time required in excess of eight cumulative hours, since that large of a request may cause some delay or disruption of the other responsibilities of the custodian's office, except that the fee for records shall not include any charge for the services of an attorney or any other person to review the requested public records seeking a legal basis to withhold the public records from the public. | For nonresidents of Nebraska, the actual added cost used as the basis for the calculation of a fee for records may include a charge for the proportion of the existing salary or pay obligation to the public officers or employees, including a proportional charge for the services of an attorney to review the requested public records, for the time spent searching, identifying, physically redacting, copying, or reviewing such records.

verified.value: “hourly wage of an employee” — base salary, excluding benefits (annual salary ÷ required hours/year if salaried)
verified.unit: USD per hour, computed per employee
verified.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § IV.A–E
verified.source_language: “Labor” is the time (in hours) reasonably necessary to produce requested records, including the time spent locating, retrieving, reviewing, redacting, and reproducing records. “Hourly wage of an employee” is based upon the base salary of the employee and does not include benefits. If an employee is not paid on an hourly basis, the hourly wage shall be determined by dividing the employee's annual salary by the required hours to be worked per year. For example, an employee who is expected to work a 37.5 hour workweek and receives $39,000 in salary on an annual basis will be deemed to be paid $20 per hour. In calculating labor charges, a records custodian should determine the total amount of labor for each employee and subtract the labor threshold from the labor of the highest paid employee(s). The records custodian should then multiply the amount of labor for each employee by each employee's hourly wage to calculate the total amount of labor charges associated with the request.
verified.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017 (submitted to ACOG Nov. 8, 2016). Verified still posted as the operative schedule on the OORC Policies, Guidelines & Forms page as of 2026-08-19; no revision published despite § 8-4-604(a)(1)(B) 'revised at least annually'.
verified.notes: Rate is not a number: it is the actual base hourly wage (excl. benefits) of each employee reasonably necessary, using the lowest practicable wage (§ IV.A), charged only above the labor threshold (≥1 hour, § IV.C) and only for producing copies (never inspection, § I.A / § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(i)). Same computed standard for search, review/redaction and reproduction — § IV.B lists 'locating, retrieving, reviewing, redacting, and reproducing'. Locating/retrieving = search.

In addition, the Commission has also previously concluded that no provision of the FOI Act permits a public agency to charge time taken to review public records to ascertain whether they contain any information that is exempt from disclosure. It is found that the respondents arrived at the fee of $628.99 by using the hourly rate of the employee who was trained and charged with reviewing and redacting (i.e., pixelating and removing audio) from the requested video footage ($612) and copying such footage onto a flash drive ($16.99). 38. At the hearing, the respondents contended that the process of redacting video footage constitutes "formatting or programming" that changes the format of the original video and results in the creation of a new video. 39. It is found that the pixelations and removal of audio conducted by the respondents were performed using existing computer software and that the respondents did not have to develop a program or contract with an outside entity to develop a program in order to comply with the records request. 40. It is found that the respondents failed to prove that the tasks, described in paragraph 37, above, constituted formatting and programming functions within the meaning of §1-212(b)(1), G.S. 41. It is concluded that the $612 fee is not allowable under §1-212(b)(1), G.S. 42. Nevertheless, pursuant to §1-212(c), G.S., "[a] public agency may require the prepayment of any fee required or permitted under the Freedom of Information Act if such fee is estimated to be ten dollars or more..." It is found that the fee for copying the footage onto a flash drive was more than ten dollars (i.e., $16.99) and therefore the respondents were permitted to require prepayment of such fee.

Municipal example: New London PD's $612 redaction charge for body-cam video disallowed, $16.99 flash-drive cost allowed (FIC 2022-0176). Legislature has repeatedly declined to authorize a redaction fee (SB 225, 2026, not enacted).
