However, the special service charge may be imposed for this work if the volume of records and the number of potential exemptions make review and redaction of the records a time-consuming task. See Florida Institutional Legal Services v. Florida Department of Corrections, 579 So. 2d at 269. And see Agency for Health Care Administration v. Zuckerman Spaeder, LLP, 221 So. 3d 1260 (Fla. 1st DCA 2017) (prior court decisions as well as the language in s. 119.07[4], F.S., dictate that the requester, who had submitted several voluminous public records requests for records which included confidential information “should be required to pay for the cost of searching, review, and redaction of exempted information prior to production”). The following is a recommended policy for agency use: Upon receiving a request for computer-stored public records that require programming, a state agency should conform to the following policy, unless covered by another statutory fee schedule. • The calculation of fees should include only the time it takes the state employee(s) to format and program the request. • It cannot include the time it takes for the search and retrieval of the information. • The hourly salary for the state employee(s) doing the programming and formatting is an allowable charge. • Fees can not include any employee fringe benefit costs. • The cost of the media is an allowable charge (i.e., if the information is supplied on a diskette, the state agency can charge for the cost of that diskette). • If an agency uses a private company, the agency can only charge for the costs incurred for those services. NE.snippet: For a Nebraska resident's request, the actual added cost used to calculate a fee shall not include any charge for existing salary/pay obligations for the first eight cumulative hours of searching, identifying, physically

verified.unit: cumulative hours per request (residents, incl. news media regardless of domicile) — labor chargeable only for time in excess; nonresidents: chargeable from 0 hours; not paper-only (applies to searching, identifying, physically redacting, copying in any medium)
verified.source_language: For residents of Nebraska, the actual added cost used as the basis for the calculation of a fee for records shall not include any charge for the existing salary or pay obligation to the public officers or employees with respect to the first eight cumulative hours of searching, identifying, physically redacting, or copying. A special service charge reflecting the calculated labor cost may be included in the fee for time required in excess of eight cumulative hours, since that large of a request may cause some delay or disruption of the other responsibilities of the custodian's office, except that the fee for records shall not include any charge for the services of an attorney or any other person to review the requested public records seeking a legal basis to withhold the public records from the public. | For nonresidents of Nebraska, the actual added cost used as the basis for the calculation of a fee for records may include a charge for the proportion of the existing salary or pay obligation to the public officers or employees, including a proportional charge for the services of an attorney to review the requested public records, for the time spent searching, identifying, physically redacting, copying, or reviewing such records. | For purposes of sections 84-712 to 84-712.09, resident means a person domiciled in this state and includes news media without regard to domicile.
verified.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
verified.notes: Trigger = hours (not pages or dollars); threshold = eight cumulative hours; scope = searching, identifying, physically redacting, or copying (attorney/legal review never chargeable to residents). Nonresident regime: proportional salary/pay from hour zero including attorney review. 'Cumulative' is read by the AG Outline as hours 'responsive to a particular records request' (per request, not per requester-period). LB 43 (2024) raised the allowance from four to eight hours (slip law shows 'first eight four cumulative hours').

verified.value: trigger = 'extraordinary expenditure of time and effort' or record 'cannot be reproduced by ordinary document copying equipment in ordinary business size' (5(c), printed matter) OR medium/format conversion requiring extensive IT use or programming/clerical/supervisory labor (5(d)); no numeric page/hour threshold; case-by-case; must be itemized and accepted/objected to before incurred; cannot be pre-set by ordinance
verified.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(c), (d), as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2; GRC Handbook 8th ed. p.27
verified.source_language: Whenever the nature, format, manner of collation, or volume of a government record embodied in the form of printed matter to be inspected, examined, or copied pursuant to this section is such that the record cannot be reproduced by ordinary document copying equipment in ordinary business size or involves an extraordinary expenditure of time and effort to accommodate the request, the public agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplicating the record, a special service charge that shall be based upon the actual direct cost of providing the copy or copies, and such special service charge shall be reasonable. The custodian shall provide the requestor with an explanation for and an itemized list of the fees or charges. The requestor shall have the opportunity to review and object to any fee or charge prior to it being incurred. There shall be a rebuttable presumption that the fees or charges presented by the custodian are reasonable. If the requestor objects to the fees or charges, the burden of proof shall be on the requestor to demonstrate that the fees or charges are unreasonable. || If the public agency converts the record to the medium or format requested, the agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplication, a special service fee that shall be reasonable and shall be based on the cost for any extensive use of information technology, or for the labor cost of personnel providing the service, that is actually incurred by the agency or attributable to the agency for the programming, clerical, and supervisory assistance required, or both. || GRC Handbook: Actual direct cost means hourly rate of the lowest level employee capable of fulfilling the request (no fringe benefits). A special service charge is calculated on a case-by-case basis. No special service charges can be established in advance by ordinance.
verified.effective_status: Current (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5 last amended P.L.2024, c.16, s.2, effective 2024-09-03; official codified text checked 2026-08-18 shows no later amendment)
verified.notes: Labor is NEVER chargeable for ordinary requests; the statutory duplication fee excludes labor. Labor becomes chargeable only through the special service charge/fee gates. 5(c) is textually 'printed matter' (paperOnly=true for the 5(c) gate); 5(d) covers electronic conversion. No 'over N pages / N hours' threshold exists in law or guidance — the GRC 14-point analysis is the qualitative test.

verified.value: never
verified.source_language: “Actual cost” means the direct cost incurred by a governmental entity in the provision of a public record, including, without limitation, the cost of ink, toner, paper, media and postage. The term does not include a cost that a governmental entity incurs regardless of whether or not a person requests a copy of a particular public record. | Sec. 13. NY.snippet: Actual reproduction cost may include only the hourly salary attributed to the lowest-paid agency employee who has the necessary skill to prepare the copy.

verified.value: never (exception: law-enforcement/prosecutor video records)
verified.source_authority: State ex rel. Warren Newspapers v. Hutson, 1994-Ohio-5, ¶ 26; Ohio Rev. Code § 149.43(B)(1) (second paragraph, video records)
verified.source_language: Copies of public records available at actual cost without charges for labor or employee time. Ohio does not specify any charge for search and/or review time in R.C. 149.43. ... Since respondents are already compensated for performing their duties, and responding to public records requests is merely another duty, the cost set forth in R.C. 149.43(B) should not include labor costs regarding employee time. Respondents' policy to the contrary was inconsistent with that provision. Additionally, there is no evidence in the record that the charge of $5 per initial page of each separate file is tied to the actual copying costs.
verified.effective_status: Current (1994; video-record exception added eff. April 9, 2025, H.B. 315, 135th G.A.)
verified.notes: Labor is never chargeable for municipal records regardless of page count, hours, or paper/electronic format. Exception: video records prepared by a state or local law enforcement agency or prosecutor's office — staff time and overhead are within 'actual cost' (OH-9011), bounded by OH-0019. Applies to every 'public office' (state, county, city, village, township, school district — R.C. 149.43(A)(1)); Ohio runs one regime for all public bodies and has no separate state-agency fee schedule.

verified.source_language: “Labor threshold” is the first (1st) hour of labor reasonably necessary to produce requested material(s). ID.snippet: Fees for resident requests shall not exceed reasonable labor costs necessarily incurred, charged at the per-hour pay rate of the lowest-paid administrative staff employee or public official of the agency.

verified.source_language: Fees for requests made by residents shall not exceed reasonable labor costs necessarily incurred in responding to a public records request, and if charged, shall reflect the personnel and quantity of time that are reasonably necessary to process a request. Fees for requests made by residents for labor costs shall be charged at the per hour pay rate of the lowest paid administrative staff employee or public official of the public agency who is necessary and qualified to process the request. If a request from a resident requires redactions to be made by an attorney who is employed by the public agency, the rate charged shall be no more than the per hour rate of the lowest paid attorney within the public agency who is necessary and qualified to process the public records request. If a request from a resident is submitted to a public agency that does not have an attorney on staff, and requires redactions by an attorney, the rate shall be no more than the usual and customary rate of the attorney who is retained by the public agency for that purpose.

A public body may charge up to $10 for each hour spent by personnel in searching for and retrieving a requested record or examining the record for necessary redactions.

verified.unit: % (the 'direct cost' formula is 105% of program-development + retrieval-labor + medium costs) — applies ONLY to § 8(g) electronic duplicates and § 6(c) reprogramming; for paper copies § 8(d) 'actual cost' expressly excludes labor and overhead
verified.source_language: "Direct cost" means one hundred five percent (105%) of the sum of the cost of: (1) the initial development of a program, if any; (2) the labor required to retrieve electronically stored data; and (3) any medium used for electronic output; for providing a duplicate of electronically stored data onto a disk, tape, drum, or other medium of electronic data retrieval under section 8(g) of this chapter, or for reprogramming a computer system under section 6(c) of this chapter.

Charges for staff time shall not include the costs of employee benefits. … In the case of fees for copies of records, the fees shall not exceed the actual cost of furnishing the requested records, including the cost of staff time required to make the information available. Actual costs may include the cost to review and redact the requested records but shall not include incidental costs incurred by the public agency that are not attributable to furnishing the requested records.

MI.snippet: Labor for searching, locating, and examining records may not be charged at more than the hourly wage of the public body's lowest-paid employee capable of doing so, regardless of who performs the labor.

MN.snippet: When copies or electronic transmittal are requested, the responsible authority may require payment of the actual costs of searching for and retrieving the data, including employee time.

MO.snippet: The hourly fee charged for duplicating time shall not exceed the average hourly rate of pay for clerical staff of the public governmental body.

NC.snippet: When separation of confidential from nonconfidential information is necessary to permit access, the public agency bears the cost of separation.

verified.source_language: For purposes of this subsection, "actual cost" is limited to direct, chargeable costs related to the reproduction of a public record as determined by generally accepted accounting principles and does not include costs that would have been incurred by the public agency if a request to reproduce a public record had not been made. Notwithstanding the provisions of this subsection, if the request is such as to require extensive use of information technology resources or extensive clerical or supervisory assistance by personnel of the agency involved, or if producing the record in the medium requested results in a greater use of information technology resources than that established by the agency for reproduction of the volume of information requested, then the agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplication, a special service charge, which shall be reasonable and shall be based on the actual cost incurred for such extensive use of information technology resources or the labor costs of the personnel providing the services, or for a greater use of information technology resources that is actually incurred by the agency or attributable to the agency.

NV.snippet: 'Actual cost' means direct cost of providing the copy (ink, toner, paper, media, postage) and excludes any cost the entity incurs regardless of whether a copy is requested.

verified.source_language: “Actual cost” means the direct cost incurred by a governmental entity in the provision of a public record, including, without limitation, the cost of ink, toner, paper, media and postage. The term does not include a cost that a governmental entity incurs regardless of whether or not a person requests a copy of a particular public record.

verified.source_language: “Hourly wage of an employee” is based upon the base salary of the employee and does not include benefits. If an employee is not paid on an hourly basis, the hourly wage shall be determined by dividing the employee's annual salary by the required hours to be worked per year. For example, an employee who is expected to work a 37.5 hour workweek and receives $39,000 in salary on an annual basis will be deemed to be paid $20 per hour.

verified.source_language: (3) The overhead charge shall be computed at 20% of the charge made to cover any labor costs associated with a particular request. CO.snippet: After the first hour, the custodian may charge a fee for research and retrieval of public records not to exceed thirty dollars per hour.

verified.source_language: A custodian may impose a fee in response to a request for the research and retrieval of public records only if the custodian has, prior to the date of receiving the request, either posted on the custodian's website or otherwise published a written policy that specifies the applicable conditions concerning the research and retrieval of public records by the custodian, including the amount of any current fee. Under any such policy, the custodian shall not impose a charge for the first hour of time expended in connection with the research and retrieval of public records. After the first hour of time has been expended, the custodian may charge a fee for the research and retrieval of public records that shall not exceed thirty dollars per hour.

verified.source_language: This subsection applies to a school corporation and a charter school. For purposes of this subsection, "computer processing time" means the amount of time a computer takes to process a command or script to extract or copy electronically stored data that is the subject of a public records request. A school corporation or charter school may not charge a fee for the first five (5) hours required to search for records that are in an electronic format. A school corporation or charter school may charge a search fee for any time spent searching for records that are in an electronic format that exceeds five (5) hours. If the school corporation or charter school charges a search fee, the school corporation or charter school shall charge an hourly fee that does not exceed the lesser of: (1) the hourly rate of the person making the search; or (2) twenty dollars ($20) per hour. A school corporation or charter school charging an hourly fee under this subsection for searching for records that are in an electronic format may charge only for time that the person making the search actually spends in searching for the records that are in an electronic format. A school corporation or charter school may not charge for computer processing time and may not establish a minimum fee for searching for records that are in an electronic format. A school corporation or charter school shall make a good faith effort to complete a search for records that are in an electronic format that is within a reasonable time in order to minimize the amount of a search fee. The fee must be prorated to reflect any search time of less than one (1) hour.

verified.source_language: “Labor threshold” is the first (1st) hour of labor reasonably necessary to produce requested material(s). A governmental entity may adopt a higher labor threshold than one (1) hour. A records custodian is only permitted to charge for labor exceeding the labor threshold established by the governmental entity. In calculating labor charges, a records custodian should determine the total amount of labor for each employee and subtract the labor threshold from the labor of the highest paid employee(s). The records custodian should then multiply the amount of labor for each employee by each employee's hourly wage to calculate the total amount of labor charges associated with the request.

verified.source_language: Upon request for records transmission by a person seeking a copy of any public record, the custodian shall transmit a copy of the record by United States mail, other delivery service, facsimile, or electronic mail. No transmission fees may be charged to the record requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail. Within the period specified in section 24-72-203 (3)(a), the custodian shall notify the record requester that a copy of the record is available but will only be sent to the requester once the custodian either receives payment or makes arrangements for receiving payment for all costs associated with records transmission and for all other fees lawfully allowed, unless recovery of all or any portion of such costs or fees has been waived by the custodian. Upon either receiving such payment or making arrangements to receive such payment at a later date, the custodian shall send the record to the requester as soon as practicable but no more than three business days after receipt of, or making arrangements to receive, such payment.
verified.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
verified.notes: No itemized-estimate threshold exists in CORA. Structural notice recorded so the engine issues the availability-and-payment notice inside the response window.

verified.source_language: A public agency may require the prepayment of any fee required or permitted under the Freedom of Information Act if such fee is estimated to be ten dollars or more.
verified.effective_status: Current — Gen. Stat. rev. to Jan. 1, 2025; § 1-212 not in the 2026 Supplement (rev. to Jan. 1, 2026 — only § 1-210(b)(17) amended in 2025); last amended P.A. 12-205; 2026-session public acts (through P.A. 26-68) searched — none amend § 1-212
verified.notes: No duty to issue an itemized estimate or cost notice at any threshold. § 1-212(c) presupposes an estimate only as the trigger for demanding prepayment ('if such fee is estimated to be ten dollars or more'); FOIC requires that any prepayment demand rest solely on fees 'required or permitted' by the Act (FIC 2025-0213 ¶ 29). Searched: Conn. Gen. Stat. ch. 14 (FOIA) §§ 1-200 to 1-242 in full (esp. §§ 1-206, 1-210, 1-211, 1-212), 2026 Supplement ch. 14, 2024/2025 reference tables (Statutes Amended), 2026 public acts (dtSearch of PA database for '1-212'), FOIC FAQ/Citizen's Guide, FOIC final decisions FIC 2025-0213 (Mar. 25, 2026) and FIC 2022-0176 (Apr. 12, 2023), DAS BEST fee guidelines under § 1-212(b)(4), § 7-34a (town clerks). Connecticut has no administrative regulation setting FOIA fees (FOIC regs, Regs. Conn. State Agencies § 1-21j-1 et seq., govern Commission procedure only).

verified.value: respond_to_cost_inquiries; follow own estimate/invoice policy before production
verified.unit: no dollar or hour threshold in law
verified.source_authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 188 (Wootton v. Cook (1st DCA 1991); Woodard v. State (4th DCA 2004); Miami Dade College v. Nader + Museu I (3d DCA 2022); AGO 13-03)
verified.official_link: https://townofjupiterisland.com/DocumentCenter/View/959/2024-Government-in-the-Sunshine-Manual (2024 ed., opened; municipal-government mirror of the AG publication) ; current 2025 ed. canonical: https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/government-in-the-sunshine-manual.pdf (403 from this environment)
verified.source_language: In order to comply with the statutory directive that an agency provide copies of public records upon payment of the statutory fee, an agency must respond to requests for information as to copying costs. Wootton v. Cook, supra. See also Woodard v. State, 885 So. 2d 444 (Fla. 4th DCA 2004), remanding a case for further proceedings where the custodian forwarded only information relating to the statutory fee schedule rather than the total cost to copy the requested records. In Miami Dade College v. Nader + Museu I, LLLP, 47 F.L.W. D1814 (Fla. 3d DCA August 31, 2022), the court affirmed the trial court’s refusal to grant an agency’s motion to collect fees under s. 119.07(4)(d), F.S., because the agency failed to provide the requester with an estimate or invoice prior to production thereby violating both its own policies and procedures and the language of s. 119.07(4), F.S. And see AGO 13-03, in which the Attorney General’s Office strongly encouraged agencies to adopt a public records procedure that addresses imposition of special service charge.
verified.effective_status: Current guidance (2024 ed., Vol. 46; reflects statutes and case law through late 2023 — 2025 ed. exists but could not be opened; requires manual verification against the 2025 edition)
verified.notes: Statute sets no estimate threshold. Operative rules: the agency must answer requests for cost information with the total cost, not just a schedule; if the agency's own policy requires an estimate/invoice before production, collection after production can be denied when none was given (Nader + Museu). AG strongly encourages a written special-service-charge procedure (AGO 13-03).

GA.snippet: Where an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 to respond, it shall notify the requester within three business days and inform the requester of the cost estimate.

verified.source_language: In any instance in which an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 for responding to a request, the agency shall notify the requester within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days and inform the requester of the estimate of the costs, and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs.
verified.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
verified.notes: Statutory trigger the city cannot move: above $25.00 the agency 'shall notify the requester ... not to exceed three business days' with the estimate. Structural companion (GA-0023): search/retrieval may be deferred until the requester agrees to pay. 'Agency' (§ 50-18-70(b)(1) via § 50-14-1(a)(1)(B)-(C)) includes every county, municipal corporation, school district and their departments, so the figure binds municipalities directly; Georgia runs a single regime for state and local bodies.

verified.source_language: Statements of fees by a public agency shall be itemized to show the per page costs for copies, and hourly rates of employees and attorneys involved in responding to the request, and the actual time spent on the public records request. No lump sum costs shall be assigned to any public records request. If a separate fee schedule is adopted for requests from persons who are not residents or employees of residents, the separate fees for such nonresidents shall be separately identified.
verified.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
verified.notes: No dollar or hour threshold triggers an estimate. Shape: whenever fees are stated, the statement must be itemized (per-page cost, hourly rates of employees and attorneys, actual time spent); no lump sums; nonresident fees separately identified. § 74-102(9) permits (does not require) the agency to help narrow scope when a response is likely to be voluminous or require payment. No 2024–2026 change.

verified.value: no dollar/hour threshold; a fee estimate is a mandatory element of the response for commercial-purpose (Sec. 3.1(a)), recurrent-requester (Sec. 3.2(a)) and voluminous (Sec. 3.6(c)) requests; no estimate duty for ordinary requests
verified.source_language: The response shall (i) provide to the requester an estimate of the time required by the public body to provide the records requested and an estimate of the fees to be charged, which the public body may require the person to pay in full before copying the requested documents, (ii) deny the request pursuant to one or more of the exemptions set out in this Act, (iii) notify the requester that the request is unduly burdensome and extend an opportunity to the requester to attempt to reduce the request to manageable proportions, or (iv) provide the records requested.
verified.notes: Illinois gates the estimate by request CLASS, not by amount. Shape for the engine: on classifying a request as commercial / recurrent / voluminous, the response option (i) is 'an estimate of the time required ... and an estimate of the fees to be charged'. Related: Sec. 6(f)/(a-5) accounting duty after fees are imposed (IL-0037), and Sec. 6(d) — a fee inconsistent with 6(a)/(b) is a denial (IL-9004).

verified.source_language: This protects the agency from doing work that will not be picked up by a requestor. However, the requestor should also be aware of the cost related to his or her APRA request in case moving forward would be cost prohibitive, rather than having it mailed to him or her with a bill for copying and postage.
verified.effective_status: Current (advisory opinion issued July 21, 2026)
verified.notes: APRA contains no itemized-estimate or cost-notice requirement or threshold. The PAC (25-FC-326, quoted) found a violation where copies were mailed with an unannounced bill and advised that requesters 'should also be aware of the cost' — guidance, not a statutory threshold; no number. Searched: Ind. Code 5-14-3 (APRA) §§ 3, 3.3, 3.5, 6, 8, 8.1, 8.3, 8.5, 9 as reproduced in the PAC Handbook (rev. Mar. 2022) and PAC HEA 1360 (2026) statutory-additions document; PAC advisory opinions 2019–2026 citing § 5-14-3-8 (17 opinions read); PAC HEA 1360 Overview; Indiana has no administrative-code fee rule for public records (APRA delegates no rulemaking except IDOA's state-agency uniform copying fee, § 8(c)). Nothing found on this item.

KS.snippet: Upon request, the agency shall provide an itemized statement of costs charged to the requester, including the hourly rates for each employee involved and an itemized list of any other fees.

verified.unit: hours of staff time | USD (estimated actual cost of staff time) — whichever is exceeded
verified.source_language: When the staff time needed to respond to a records request will exceed five hours or the estimated actual cost for staff time needed to fill the request exceeds $200, the public agency shall make reasonable efforts to contact the requester and engage in interactive communication about mitigating costs to fill the request. The requester is not obligated to mitigate costs. … Upon request, a public agency shall provide to the person requesting access to or copies of public records pursuant to this section an itemized statement of costs incurred by the public agency and charged to such requester. Such itemized statement shall include, but not be limited to, the hourly rates charged for each employee involved in making the requested records available and an itemized list of any other fees charged to provide access to or furnish copies of the requested records.
verified.effective_status: Effective 2025-07-01 (L. 2025, ch. 89, § 1 [HB 2134]); no 2026 amendment
verified.notes: Shape differs from a classic itemized-estimate trigger: above the threshold the agency 'shall make reasonable efforts to contact the requester and engage in interactive communication about mitigating costs' ('reasonable efforts' = using the contact means the requester provided, (e)(3)); the requester need not mitigate. There is no separate statutory dollar trigger for a written estimate — an itemized statement of costs is owed 'upon request' at any amount ((c)(4), KS-0039), and advance payment may be required at any amount (KS-0043). Both thresholds are staff-time-only (not total cost).

verified.value: advance notice of the fee amount before production; no dollar/hour threshold
verified.source_language: For all public records, except public records of state agencies, it shall be the duty of the custodian of the public records to provide copies to persons so requesting, unless the requestor fails to pay the applicable copying fees after being notified of the amount in advance of production or the requestor has an outstanding balance from a prior request.
verified.effective_status: Current (last amended Acts 2024, No. 411; fee text of (C)(1)(a) as amended by Acts 2023, No. 247, eff. Aug. 1, 2023; no 2025 or 2026 amendment found)
verified.notes: The nonpayment excuse operates only 'after being notified of the amount in advance of production' — so a fee-amount notice must precede production whenever a fee will be collected; there is no threshold above which an itemized estimate is required and no itemization requirement. R.S. 44:35(A) references an 'estimate of the time reasonably necessary for collection, segregation, redaction, examination, or review' — a time estimate, not a cost estimate. State agencies only: LAC 4:I.301.D requires a cost estimate for programming-dependent computer records (LA-9004).

MA.snippet: If fees are to be assessed, the RAO must provide a written, itemized, good-faith estimate of fees before complying, within the 10-business-day response.

MI.snippet: A public body's procedures must use a standard form for detailed itemization of any fee that clearly lists and explains the allowable charges for each of the six fee components used in estimating or charging.

MO.snippet: A requester may request an estimate of the cost of copies before the public body produces them.

verified.source_authority: N.C. Gen. Stat. ch. 132 (searched); N.C. Attorney General, Open Government Guide (2019) p. 10 (best practice)
verified.source_language: As a best practice, notify the requesting party in writing that the request has been received and give a reasonable timetable for a response. If this is a request for which fees might be charged, include information about those costs, but check with your agency's public records staff to make sure it is charging that kind of fee.
verified.effective_status: Current as posted (2019 edition, Attorney General Josh Stein / N.C. Press Association; guidance, not law; predates the Jan. 2025 change of Attorney General — no later edition located)
verified.notes: No statutory or regulatory itemized-estimate / cost-notice threshold. The AG Guide's advisory best practice (include cost information in a written acknowledgment) is 'should'-level guidance, recorded as NC-9011 for the notice shape only — it sets no dollar or hour threshold. Searched: N.C. Gen. Stat. ch. 132 (Public Records) in full at ncleg.gov (current through S.L. 2026-30), incl. §§ 132-1(b), 132-6, 132-6.1, 132-6.2, 132-1.4A(l), 132-10; ch. 159 (§ 159-32.1); ncleg 'Law modifications not yet reflected in statute' (2026); N.C. Attorney General 2019 Open Government Guide (ncdoj.gov, 'Charging Fees' section); Governor's Office 'Guidance for Public Records and Meetings Access' (July 2018); ncdoj.gov Legal Opinions Directory (search 'public records fee' — no fee opinion surfaced; the 'Public Records' opinion page returned a WordPress error); no N.C. Administrative Code title governs municipal public-records fees (agency-specific NCAC fee rules exist only for the promulgating agency).

NE.snippet: With its timely response, the custodian must provide the requester an estimate of the expected cost of the copies.

verified.unit: USD (estimate required with every response, no threshold)
verified.source_language: Upon receipt of a written request for access to or copies of a public record, the custodian of such record shall provide to the requester as soon as is practicable and without delay, but not more than four business days after actual receipt of the request, an estimate of the expected cost of the copies and either (a) access to or, if copying equipment is reasonably available, copies of the public record, (b) if there is a legal basis for denial of access or copies, a written denial of the request together with the information specified in section 84-712.04, or (c) if the entire request cannot with reasonable good faith efforts be fulfilled within four business days after actual receipt of the request due to the significant difficulty or the extensiveness of the request, a written explanation, including the earliest practicable date for fulfilling the request, an estimate of the expected cost of any copies, and an opportunity for the requester to modify or prioritize the items within the request.
verified.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
verified.notes: The estimate of expected copy cost is a mandatory component of the custodian's response to every written request (within four business days) — there is no dollar or hour threshold below which it may be omitted; when the request cannot be fulfilled in four business days the delay explanation must also include the estimate. Engine shape: always emit an estimate; the estimate opens the requester's ten-business-day review window.

verified.value: any fee or charge (no dollar/hour threshold): custodian shall provide an explanation and itemized list of fees or charges; requestor may review and object before the charge is incurred; GRC: special service charge estimate must be given in advance and processing awaits written acceptance
verified.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(c), as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2; GRC Handbook 8th ed. p.27
verified.source_language: The custodian shall provide the requestor with an explanation for and an itemized list of the fees or charges. The requestor shall have the opportunity to review and object to any fee or charge prior to it being incurred. There shall be a rebuttable presumption that the fees or charges presented by the custodian are reasonable. If the requestor objects to the fees or charges, the burden of proof shall be on the requestor to demonstrate that the fees or charges are unreasonable. || GRC Handbook: The custodian must notify the requestor in advance of the special service charge. Under P.L. 2024, c.16, custodians are now required to include as part of their response “an explanation for and an itemized list of the fees or charges” associated with the assessed fee at the time it is provided to the requestor. N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(c).
verified.effective_status: Current (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5 last amended P.L.2024, c.16, s.2, effective 2024-09-03; official codified text checked 2026-08-18 shows no later amendment)
verified.notes: Itemization/objection duty is unconditional in the statute (all 'fees or charges'); in practice it operates whenever a special service charge/fee, media cost or deposit is assessed. Also 5(f): the request form must state the fees to be charged and whether prepayment/deposit is required (NJ-M14). No numeric threshold anywhere.

verified.source_authority: Nev. Admin. Code § 239.864(1) (Executive Department agencies only); Nev. Rev. Stat. § 239.008(3)
verified.source_language: If an agency of the Executive Department charges a fee for providing a copy of a public record: 1. A records official shall provide a person who requests a copy of a public record with an estimate of the fee for the copy, if the estimated actual cost is more than $25. The estimate of the fee must include, without limitation, the amount of postage that the agency will charge the person if the person requested to have the copy delivered by mail.
verified.effective_status: Current (NAC 239.864 added R107-13, eff. 12-22-2014; no later amendment)
verified.notes: State-agency regime: a records official of an agency of the Executive Department shall give a written estimate when estimated actual cost exceeds $25 (NAC 239.864(1); NAC 239.863(1)(f)(2) mirrors it on the request form). NAC 239.860-.869 are adopted under NRS 239.008(3), which reaches only 'an agency of the Executive Department' - they do not bind cities, counties or school districts. Municipal regime: no estimate threshold; a city adopting one may look to the $25 agency figure as guidance.

NY.snippet: The requester shall be informed of the estimated cost of preparing the copy if more than two hours of employee time is needed or if an outside professional service would be retained.

verified.source_authority: Ohio Attorney General, 2026 Ohio Sunshine Laws: An Open Government Resource Manual, ch. 2, § 12 'Copies, and delivery or transmission, "at cost"' (pp. 21-22) (citing State ex rel. Ware v. City of Akron, 2021-Ohio-624); Ohio Rev. Code § 149.43(B)(1) (video records)
verified.source_language: There is no obligation to provide free copies to someone who cannot or will not pay. However, before denying a request for failure to pay, the public office must first inform the requester of the amount due. | A state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office shall provide the requester with the estimated actual cost within five business days of receipt of the public records request.
verified.effective_status: Current (manual 2026 edition; video estimate rule eff. April 9, 2025)
verified.notes: No dollar/hour threshold triggers an itemized estimate for general municipal records. Structural rules instead: (1) a cost notice (amount due) must precede any denial for nonpayment (OH-9014); (2) law-enforcement/prosecutor video: estimated actual cost within five business days of receipt (OH-9009, statute). Ohio law does not require itemization.

OR.snippet: A public body may not establish a fee greater than $25 unless it first provides the requester written notification of the estimated fee amount and the requester confirms that it wants the public body to proceed.

verified.value: no dollar/hour threshold — an estimate of applicable fees is a required element of every § 902 extension notice; prepayment of the estimate may be required only when fees are expected to exceed $100
verified.unit: USD (none for the notice; $100 for prepayment)
verified.source_language: The notice shall include a statement notifying the requester that the request for access is being reviewed, the reason for the review, a reasonable date that a response is expected to be provided and an estimate of applicable fees owed when the record becomes available.
verified.effective_status: Current — § 1307 unamended since enactment (Act 3 of 2008); compiled text reflects amendments through Act 29 of 2023; no 2024–2026 enacted amendment to §§ 901–905 or 1307 found
verified.notes: The engine should emit a fee estimate with any extension notice regardless of amount. No separate itemization requirement found. Prior status 'silent' was wrong.

verified.source_language: A deposit not to exceed twenty-five percent of the total reasonably anticipated cost for reproduction of the records may be required prior to the public body searching for or making copies of records.
verified.effective_status: Current (2017 Act No. 67, eff. May 19, 2017; no later amendment through 2025 session; no 2026 act found)
verified.notes: No itemized-estimate or cost-notice requirement and no dollar/hour threshold. The deposit clause presupposes a 'total reasonably anticipated cost' but imposes no notice duty. The AG's own office states its fee 'will be shared prior to the processing of a request' — agency procedure, not law. Searched: S.C. Code Title 30 ch. 4 (FOIA, all sections; fee content confined to § 30-4-30(B)-(C)); S.C. Code of Regulations index and ch. 12 (Archives & History) — no FOIA fee regulation exists; SC Attorney General FOIA page and opinion search (scag.gov/search: 'FOIA fee 30-4-30', 'prorated hourly salary', 'prevailing commercial rate', 'FOIA redaction fee') — opened AG Ops. of June 28, 2019 (Forrest/Hudson), Jan. 24, 2020 (McCurdy, clerks of court), May 31, 2024 (Swindler, BWC); 2024, 2025 and 2026 Acts lists on scstatehouse.gov (no FOIA fee act); S. 6 (2025-2026) which re-states § 30-4-30(B) unchanged and remains in Senate Judiciary.

citations: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B); OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.G; OORC Model Public Records Policy § VI.B
TN.snippet: The records custodian shall provide the requestor an estimate of the reasonable costs to provide copies of the requested material before producing them.

verified.unit: USD (an estimate of reasonable costs is required before any copy charge, at any amount; model policy: itemized)
verified.source_authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)(ii); OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.G; OORC Model Public Records Policy § VI.B
verified.source_language: (ii) The records custodian shall provide a requestor an estimate of the reasonable costs to provide copies of the requested material. [Schedule § I.G:] G. Records custodians shall provide a requestor an estimate of reasonable costs to provide copies of requested records. [Model Policy § VI.B:] B. Records custodians shall provide requestors with an itemized estimate of the charges [using Form __] prior to producing copies of records and may require pre-payment of such charges before producing requested records.
verified.effective_status: Current (FindLaw reproduction current through Jan. 2, 2024; OORC 2024 and 2025 Legislative Updates report no amendment to these provisions; 2026 session: no fee amendment found, OORC Fall 2026 update not yet published)
verified.notes: No dollar or hours threshold — the estimate duty is unconditional whenever charges will be assessed; OORC FAQ: no charge may be collected until the estimate is given (TN-9014). The OORC request form lets a requestor waive the estimate by agreeing to pay up to a stated amount.

TX.snippet: If a copy charge (or a § 552.271 paper-inspection charge) will exceed $40, the body must give the requestor a written itemized statement detailing all estimated charges (including labor/personnel), notice of any less-cos

verified.unit: USD — written itemized statement of estimated charges required when the copy charge (or § 552.271 paper-inspection charge) will exceed $40
verified.source_language: (a) If a request for a copy of public information will result in the imposition of a charge under this subchapter that exceeds $40, or a request to inspect a paper record will result in the imposition of a charge under Section 552.271 that exceeds $40, the governmental body shall provide the requestor with a written itemized statement that details all estimated charges that will be imposed, including any allowable charges for labor or personnel costs.
verified.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
verified.notes: Fixed statutory trigger; failure to send the statement caps collection at $40 (1 TAC § 70.7(a), TX-9018). A separate, threshold-free statement applies to programming/manipulation requests (§ 552.231, TX-9038).

verified.source_authority: Utah Code § 63G-2-203(8)(a) (searched); Utah Division of Archives and Records Service, GRAMA Request Form & GRAMA Request for Payment or Prepayment (2025)
verified.source_language: (coverage note — no statutory threshold above which an itemized estimate/cost notice must be issued) | (8)(a) A governmental entity may require payment of past fees and future estimated fees before beginning to process a request if: (i) fees are expected to exceed $50; or (ii) after the government entity has sent an invoice, the requester has not paid fees from a previous request. (b) Any prepaid amount in excess of fees due shall be returned to the requester. | Official form: Do you want to be contacted if the cost of providing records exceeds a certain amount? Yes / No. If yes, state the amount | Official form: Note: Utah Code § 63G-2-203(1) & (8) provides that a governmental entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover the actual cost of providing a record(s). Prepayment may be required if the cost exceeds $50 or if the requester has not paid for previous requests after an invoice has been sent. Additionally, requesters may ask for a cost estimate before authorizing a governmental entity to process a request.
verified.effective_status: Current (63G-2-203 last amended Ch. 33 (S.B. 188), 2025 General Session, effective 3/17/2025 — technical wording change to (8)(a)(ii) only; no 2026 General Session amendment as of 2026-08-19)
verified.notes: GRAMA imposes no estimate-notice duty or threshold. The $50 figure in § 63G-2-203(8)(a)(i) is a PREPAYMENT trigger, not an estimate-notice threshold (do not conflate). Official Archives forms supply the practice: the GRAMA Request Form lets the requester name an amount above which they want to be contacted, and the payment form states 'requesters may ask for a cost estimate before authorizing a governmental entity to process a request' — guidance, not law. § 63G-2-204(7)(c)(ii) requires an estimate of TIME (not cost) in voluminous-request extraordinary circumstances. Searched: Utah Code § 63G-2-203 (all subsections, current text as amended 2025), §§ 63G-2-201, -204, -209, -401, -701; Utah Municipal Code § 10-8-85.6; 2024–2026 General Session passed-bill lists (records/fee bills); Utah Division of Archives and Records Service GRAMA FAQ, guidelines page, and official forms (GRAMA Request Form; GRAMA Request for Payment or Prepayment 2025); Government Records Office decision 2024-202. No Utah Administrative Code rule sets GRAMA fees for political subdivisions; the AG issues no GRAMA fee opinions/schedule binding cities.

VA.snippet: Prior to conducting a search for records, the body shall notify the requester in writing that it may make reasonable charges not to exceed actual cost and inquire whether the requester would like a cost estimate in advan

citations: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(a)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
AL.snippet: If the public officer elects to charge a fee for a standard request, the officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment.

verified.source_language: The requester may opt not to pay the fee and thus not receive any substantive response. | The public officer shall notify the requester within 15 business days after acknowledging receipt that the request qualifies as a time-intensive request. At that time, the public officer shall notify the requester of any likely fees and allow the requester to withdraw the time-intensive request and submit a new request that is not a time-intensive request.
verified.effective_status: Current; Act 2024-278 effective October 1, 2024; no amendment to the fee provisions in the 2025 or 2026 Regular Sessions (codified history through Act 2026-592 shows only Act 2024-278)
verified.notes: No statutory response window after an estimate: the requester 'may opt not to pay' (no deadline, no deemed-withdrawal); a time-intensive requester may withdraw and resubmit, again with no deadline stated. Official link is the Legislature's Code of Alabama viewer (browse Title 36 > Chapter 12 > Article 3; section text also served by its GraphQL endpoint https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql, query codeOfAlabamaSection); alternate direct text: enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF.

verified.source_authority: Ariz. Rev. Stat. Title 39, ch. 1, art. 2
verified.source_language: The custodian of such records shall promptly furnish such copies, printouts or photographs and may charge a fee if the facilities are available, except that public records for purposes listed in section 39-122 or 39-127 shall be furnished without charge.

verified.source_language: Upon request for records transmission by a person seeking a copy of any public record, the custodian shall transmit a copy of the record by United States mail, other delivery service, facsimile, or electronic mail. No transmission fees may be charged to the record requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail. Within the period specified in section 24-72-203 (3)(a), the custodian shall notify the record requester that a copy of the record is available but will only be sent to the requester once the custodian either receives payment or makes arrangements for receiving payment for all costs associated with records transmission and for all other fees lawfully allowed, unless recovery of all or any portion of such costs or fees has been waived by the custodian. Upon either receiving such payment or making arrangements to receive such payment at a later date, the custodian shall send the record to the requester as soon as practicable but no more than three business days after receipt of, or making arrangements to receive, such payment.

GA.snippet: Where an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 to respond, it shall notify the requester within three business days and inform the requester of the cost estimate.

verified.source_language: In any instance in which an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 for responding to a request, the agency shall notify the requester within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days and inform the requester of the estimate of the costs, and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs.

AL.snippet: If the public officer elects to charge a fee for a standard request, the officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment.

verified.source_language: Records requested: (Be as specific as possible. A public officer is not obligated to respond to a request that is vague, ambiguous, overly broad, or unreasonable in scope, nor is a public officer obligated to respond to a request that seeks records that do not exist or materials that are not public records. Additionally, extensive requests for public records may increase the fees to cover the administrative cost of searching and copying the requested records.) [...] Payment of fees may be required before your request is fulfilled.
verified.effective_status: Current; Act 2024-278 effective October 1, 2024; no amendment to the fee provisions in the 2025 or 2026 Regular Sessions (codified history through Act 2026-592 shows only Act 2024-278)
verified.notes: No revised-estimate trigger or percentage; the default form only warns that extensive requests 'may increase the fees'. Official link is the Legislature's Code of Alabama viewer (browse Title 36 > Chapter 12 > Article 3; section text also served by its GraphQL endpoint https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql, query codeOfAlabamaSection); alternate direct text: enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF.

verified.source_language: Each agency, upon a request for a copy of records, shall, within 10 days from receipt of the request, determine whether the request, in whole or in part, seeks copies of disclosable public records in the possession of the agency and shall promptly notify the person making the request of the determination and the reasons therefor. If the agency determines that the request seeks disclosable public records, the agency shall also state the estimated date and time when the records will be made available.

GA.snippet: Where an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 to respond, it shall notify the requester within three business days and inform the requester of the cost estimate.

verified.source_language: In any instance in which an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 for responding to a request, the agency shall notify the requester within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days and inform the requester of the estimate of the costs, and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs.

KS.snippet: Upon request, the agency shall provide an itemized statement of costs charged to the requester, including the hourly rates for each employee involved and an itemized list of any other fees.

verified.source_language: Upon request, a public agency shall provide to the person requesting access to or copies of public records pursuant to this section an itemized statement of costs incurred by the public agency and charged to such requester. Such itemized statement shall include, but not be limited to, the hourly rates charged for each employee involved in making the requested records available and an itemized list of any other fees charged to provide access to or furnish copies of the requested records.

NY.snippet: The requester shall be informed of the estimated cost of preparing the copy if more than two hours of employee time is needed or if an outside professional service would be retained.

verified.unit: % of estimated actual cost — law-enforcement/prosecutor VIDEO RECORDS ONLY (overrun collectible up to this cap, only with advance notice); no rule for other municipal records
verified.source_language: If the actual cost exceeds the estimated actual cost, a state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office may charge a requester for the difference upon fulfilling a request for video records if the requester is notified in advance that the actual cost may be up to twenty per cent higher than the estimated actual cost. A state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office shall not charge a requester a difference that exceeds twenty per cent of the estimated actual cost.
verified.effective_status: Current (video-record cost language added eff. April 9, 2025 by H.B. 315, 135th G.A.; carried unchanged in the Sept. 30, 2025 (H.B. 96) and Sept. 7, 2026 (H.B. 31) versions)
verified.notes: Record-specific: state or local law enforcement agencies and prosecuting attorneys' offices only (municipal police departments included). Not a rule for the city's other records. Ohio's mechanism is not a 'revised estimate': the agency may bill the difference on fulfillment if it warned in advance that actual cost may run up to 20% over the estimate, and may never bill more than 20% over. For non-video municipal records the statute, manual and model policy are silent (no estimate at all is required).

TX.snippet: If a copy charge (or a § 552.271 paper-inspection charge) will exceed $40, the body must give the requestor a written itemized statement detailing all estimated charges (including labor/personnel), notice of any less-cos

verified.unit: % — updated written itemized statement required when, before the copy is made available, estimated charges will exceed the prior statement by 20 percent or more
verified.source_language: (c) If the governmental body later determines, but before it makes the copy or the paper record available, that the estimated charges will exceed the charges detailed in the written itemized statement by 20 percent or more, the governmental body shall send to the requestor a written updated itemized statement that details all estimated charges that will be imposed, including any allowable charges for labor or personnel costs. If the requestor does not respond in writing to the updated estimate in the time and manner described by Subsection (b), the request is considered to have been withdrawn by the requestor.

AL.snippet: For a time-intensive request, the public officer shall require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before providing a substantive response.

verified.value: no dollar threshold; officer discretion (standard) / mandatory prepayment (time-intensive)
verified.source_language: The public officer may require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before the requester may receive any public records. If the public officer elects to charge a fee, the public officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment. The requester may opt not to pay the fee and thus not receive any substantive response. Additionally, the public officer shall have the discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records. | The public officer shall require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before providing a substantive response to the requester. The public officer shall notify the requester in advance of any likely fees and shall withhold any substantive response until receipt of payment. Additionally, the public officer shall have the discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records.
verified.effective_status: Current; Act 2024-278 effective October 1, 2024; no amendment to the fee provisions in the 2025 or 2026 Regular Sessions (codified history through Act 2026-592 shows only Act 2024-278)
verified.notes: Prepayment of 'all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching' is at the officer's discretion for every request regardless of amount (no threshold); for time-intensive requests payment of the reasonable fee before any substantive response is mandatory. A city may set its own threshold under the officer's discretion. Official link is the Legislature's Code of Alabama viewer (browse Title 36 > Chapter 12 > Article 3; section text also served by its GraphQL endpoint https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql, query codeOfAlabamaSection); alternate direct text: enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF.

Engine: prepayment gate keyed on delivery=mail (and on commercial purpose), threshold = none.

Section 1-212(c), G.S., limits a public agency's ability to request prepayment of fees to only those fees that are required or permitted under the FOI Act. See §1-212(c), G.S. ("[a] public agency may require prepayment of any fee required or permitted under the [FOI] Act, if such fee is estimated to be ten dollars or more.") (Emphasis added).
verified.effective_status: Current — Gen. Stat. rev. to Jan. 1, 2025; § 1-212 not in the 2026 Supplement (rev. to Jan. 1, 2026 — only § 1-210(b)(17) amended in 2025); last amended P.A. 12-205; 2026-session public acts (through P.A. 26-68) searched — none amend § 1-212
verified.notes: Fixed statutory threshold ($10 estimated fee), discretionary invocation ('may require'). Connecticut's device is full PREPAYMENT, not a partial deposit. Prepayment may be predicated only on fees the Act permits (FIC 2025-0213 ¶¶ 29, 76-78) and not on costs that would have to be waived under § 1-212(d)(2) (¶¶ 74-75). Municipal example: New London PD could require prepayment of the $16.99 flash-drive fee (FIC 2022-0176 ¶ 42).

verified.unit: no statutory dollar threshold; deposit/advance payment permitted under a reasonable agency policy for extensive/voluminous requests
verified.source_authority: § 119.07(4), Fla. Stat. (introductory clause); Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 187 (Colby (2d DCA 2008); Morris Publishing (1st DCA 2015); Dorchester Holdings (2d DCA 2021); Promenade D'Iberville (1st DCA 2014))
verified.official_link: https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/119.07 ; https://townofjupiterisland.com/DocumentCenter/View/959/2024-Government-in-the-Sunshine-Manual (2024 ed., opened; municipal-government mirror of the AG publication) ; current 2025 ed. canonical: https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/government-in-the-sunshine-manual.pdf (403 from this environment)
verified.source_language: The custodian of public records shall furnish a copy or a certified copy of the record upon payment of the fee prescribed by law. If a fee is not prescribed by law, the following fees are authorized: || Section 119.07(4)(a)1., F.S., states that the custodian of public records shall furnish a copy or a certified copy of the record “upon payment of the fee prescribed by law . . . .” See Wootton v. Cook, 590 So. 2d 1039, 1040 (Fla. 1st DCA 1991) (if a requestor “identifies a record with sufficient specificity to permit [the agency] to identify it and forwards the appropriate fee, [the agency] must furnish by mail a copy of the record.”) (e.s.); and Promenade D’Iberville, LLC v. Sundy 145 So. 3d 980, 983 (Fla. 1st DCA 2014) (a records custodian may delay production “if the requesting party fails to remit the appropriate fees”). Accordingly, an agency’s policy of requiring the payment of a deposit prior to redaction and delivery of hundreds of telephone recordings related to a criminal trial was determined to be “facially reasonable.” Morris Publishing Group, LLC v. State, 154 So. 3d 528, 534 (Fla. 1st DCA 2015), review denied, 163 So. 3d 512 (Fla. 2015). Accord Board of County Commissioners of Highlands County v. Colby, 976 So. 2d 31, 37 (Fla. 2d DCA 2008), noting that a “policy of requiring an advance deposit seems prudent given the legislature’s determination that taxpayers should not shoulder the entire expense of responding to an extensive request for public records.” “[T]he reasonableness of a policy and its application — based on the facts in a particular case — guides whether an abuse of discretion is shown.” Morris Publishing Group, LLC at 534. And see Agency for Health Care Administration v. Zuckerman Spaeder, LLP, 221 So. 3d 1260 (Fla. 1st DCA 2017) (lower court abused its discretion by ordering the agency to produce a large number of responsive public records within 48 hours of the issuance of the order without requiring advance payment of the agency’s invoices associated with production of the records); City of St. Petersburg v. Dorchester Holdings, LLC, 331 So. 3d 799 (Fla. 2d DCA 2021) (trial court erred in holding that the City’s prepayment request constituted an unlawful interference with requester’s right of access to public records).
verified.effective_status: Current (2025 Florida Statutes; s. 119.07 last amended s. 1, ch. 2021-173; no 2024, 2025 or 2026 amendment to subsection (4) — CS/HB 437 (2026), which would have restricted fees, authorized waivers and required written cost estimates, passed the House 111-0 on 3/4/2026 and died in Senate Rules 3/13/2026)
verified.notes: The threshold is whatever the city's written policy sets, subject to reasonableness; nothing in law fixes a dollar figure. State-agency regime example: DOS requires prepayment of the full estimated special service charge (r. 1-2.0031(2)(b), FL-9002).

GA.snippet: Where the estimated production cost exceeds $500.00, the agency may insist on prepayment of the costs before beginning search, retrieval, review, or production.

verified.unit: USD (estimated costs for production of the records)
verified.source_language: In any instance in which the estimated costs for production of the records exceeds $500.00, an agency may insist on prepayment of the costs prior to beginning search, retrieval, review, or production of the records.
verified.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
verified.notes: Above $500.00 the agency 'may insist on prepayment of the costs' before beginning search, retrieval, review or production. Below that threshold prepayment cannot be insisted upon, though search/retrieval may still be deferred pending agreement to pay once the estimate exceeds $25 (GA-0023). Threshold is fixed by statute; the city only chooses whether to exercise the permission. 'Agency' (§ 50-18-70(b)(1) via § 50-14-1(a)(1)(B)-(C)) includes every county, municipal corporation, school district and their departments, so the figure binds municipalities directly; Georgia runs a single regime for state and local bodies.

verified.source_language: The public officer may require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before the requester may receive any public records. If the public officer elects to charge a fee, the public officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment. The requester may opt not to pay the fee and thus not receive any substantive response. Additionally, the public officer shall have the discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records. | The public officer shall require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before providing a substantive response to the requester. The public officer shall notify the requester in advance of any likely fees and shall withhold any substantive response until receipt of payment. Additionally, the public officer shall have the discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records.

verified.source_language: Upon request for records transmission by a person seeking a copy of any public record, the custodian shall transmit a copy of the record by United States mail, other delivery service, facsimile, or electronic mail. No transmission fees may be charged to the record requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail. Within the period specified in section 24-72-203 (3)(a), the custodian shall notify the record requester that a copy of the record is available but will only be sent to the requester once the custodian either receives payment or makes arrangements for receiving payment for all costs associated with records transmission and for all other fees lawfully allowed, unless recovery of all or any portion of such costs or fees has been waived by the custodian. Upon either receiving such payment or making arrangements to receive such payment at a later date, the custodian shall send the record to the requester as soon as practicable but no more than three business days after receipt of, or making arrangements to receive, such payment.

verified.source_language: In any instance in which an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 for responding to a request, the agency shall notify the requester within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days and inform the requester of the estimate of the costs, and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs. In any instance in which the estimated costs for production of the records exceeds $500.00, an agency may insist on prepayment of the costs prior to beginning search, retrieval, review, or production of the records. Whenever any person has requested to inspect or copy a public record and does not pay the cost for search, retrieval, redaction, or copying of such records when such charges have been lawfully estimated and agreed to pursuant to this article, and the agency has incurred the agreed-upon costs to make the records available, regardless of whether the requester inspects or accepts copies of the records, the agency shall be authorized to collect such charges in any manner authorized by law for the collection of taxes, fees, or assessments by such agency.

Practical effect of § 1-212(c): copies need not be released until a properly estimated fee ≥ $10 is prepaid; if the prepayment demand rests on impermissible fees, withholding is a denial (FIC 2025-0213 fn. 7). Searched: Conn. Gen. Stat. ch. 14 (FOIA) §§ 1-200 to 1-242 in full (esp. §§ 1-206, 1-210, 1-211, 1-212), 2026 Supplement ch. 14, 2024/2025 reference tables (Statutes Amended), 2026 public acts (dtSearch of PA database for '1-212'), FOIC FAQ/Citizen's Guide, FOIC final decisions FIC 2025-0213 (Mar. 25, 2026) and FIC 2022-0176 (Apr. 12, 2023), DAS BEST fee guidelines under § 1-212(b)(4), § 7-34a (town clerks). verified.value: withhold_further_records_until_prior_balance_paid; no_permanent_ban; bill_deposit_shortfall
verified.source_authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 187-188 (Lozman v. City of Riviera Beach (4th DCA 2008); Smith v. State (2d DCA 2022); AGO 05-28)
verified.official_link: https://townofjupiterisland.com/DocumentCenter/View/959/2024-Government-in-the-Sunshine-Manual (2024 ed., opened; municipal-government mirror of the AG publication) ; current 2025 ed. canonical: https://www.myfloridalegal.com/sites/default/files/government-in-the-sunshine-manual.pdf (403 from this environment)
verified.source_language: An agency may refuse to produce additional records if the fees for a previous request for records have not been paid by the requestor. See Lozman v. City of Riviera Beach, 995 So. 2d 1027 (Fla. 4th DCA 2008) (s. 119.07[4], F.S., “does not require the City to do any more than what it did in this case,” i.e., require Lozman to pay the bill for the first group of records he requested before the city would make any further documents available). And see AGO 05-28 (custodian authorized to bill the requestor for any shortfall between the deposit and the actual cost of copying the public records when the copies have been made and the requesting party subsequently advises the city that the records are not needed). Compare, Smith v. State, 335 So. 3d 795 (Fla. 2d DCA 2022) (Smith’s failure to timely pay fees to obtain requested public records does not permit the agency to ban him from ever obtaining records in the future, provided Smith pays the amount owing for the first request).
verified.effective_status: Current guidance (2024 ed., Vol. 46; reflects statutes and case law through late 2023 — 2025 ed. exists but could not be opened; requires manual verification against the 2025 edition)
verified.notes: Prior-debt prepayment: permitted (city case, Lozman) but not a lifetime ban (Smith). Florida law has no 'request deemed withdrawn after N days of nonpayment' rule — that is a city-policy matter.

GA.snippet: Where a requester has not paid costs lawfully incurred for a prior request, the agency may require prepayment for all future requests from that person until the prior costs are paid or the payment dispute is resolved.

verified.value: prior_unpaid_costs -> may require prepayment for all future requests until paid or dispute resolved; no deemed-withdrawal-after-N-days rule
verified.source_language: Whenever any person who has requested to inspect or copy a public record has not paid the cost for search, retrieval, redaction, or copying of such records when such charges have been lawfully incurred, an agency may require prepayment for compliance with all future requests for production of records from that person until the costs for the prior production of records have been paid or the dispute regarding payment resolved. Whenever any person has requested to inspect or copy a public record and does not pay the cost for search, retrieval, redaction, or copying of such records when such charges have been lawfully estimated and agreed to pursuant to this article, and the agency has incurred the agreed-upon costs to make the records available, regardless of whether the requester inspects or accepts copies of the records, the agency shall be authorized to collect such charges in any manner authorized by law for the collection of taxes, fees, or assessments by such agency.
verified.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
verified.notes: Georgia has no N-day nonpayment withdrawal clock; the consequences are (i) requester-level prepayment gating for future requests (GA-0025) and (ii) collection of agreed, incurred costs 'in any manner authorized by law for the collection of taxes, fees, or assessments' (GA-0026).

verified.effective_status: Current (am. 2025, ch. 298 [H0253], eff. July 1, 2025; no 2026 amendment — legislature.idaho.gov codified text updated July 1, 2026 shows last amendment 2025 ch. 298)
verified.notes: No withdrawn-after-N-days rule and no prior-debt prepayment rule. Searched: Idaho Code Title 74 ch. 1 (§§ 74-101 to 74-127, opened §§ 74-101, -102, -103, -113, -115, -120 on legislature.idaho.gov, codified text updated July 1, 2026); Title 50 ch. 9 (§§ 50-907, 50-908) and Title 63 (§§ 63-1311, 63-1311A); AG Idaho Public Records Law Manual (July 2026 edition, Q&A 13-17 and the AG legal-guideline index at p. 69); 2025 session (H0253 = ch. 298) and 2026 session bill list (no fee bill enacted; only H0894 open-meetings recording became law); IDAPA search for a general public-records fee rule binding local agencies (none; only agency-specific schedules such as IDAPA 16.02.08.251, which bind that agency only).

verified.value: voluminous requests: unpaid Sec. 6 fee is 'a debt due and owing to the public body' collectible under applicable law, chargeable even if records are not accepted/collected; no withdrawal-after-N-days rule; no prior-debt prepayment rule; silent for other request classes
verified.source_language: If a requester does not pay a fee charged pursuant to Section 6 of this Act for a voluminous request, the debt shall be considered a debt due and owing to the public body and may be collected in accordance with applicable law. This fee may be charged by the public body even if the requester fails to accept or collect records the public body has prepared in response to a voluminous request.
verified.effective_status: Current (Sec. 3.6 P.A. 98-1129 eff. 12-3-14; no later amendment)
verified.notes: The Sec. 3.6(a) voluminous notice must warn of this consequence (item (viii)). Nothing in the Act deems a request withdrawn for nonpayment or authorizes refusing a new request over an old debt.

verified.source_language: A public agency may require that the payment for search and copying costs be made in advance.
verified.effective_status: Current — subsection unchanged since P.L. 58-2016 per the handbook history line and quoted identically in PAC advisory opinions issued through August 2026; HEA 1360 (P.L. 97-2026, eff.
