Searched: Ind. Code 5-14-3 (APRA) §§ 3, 3.3, 3.5, 6, 8, 8.1, 8.3, 8.5, 9 as reproduced in the PAC Handbook (rev. Mar. 2022) and PAC HEA 1360 (2026) statutory-additions document; PAC advisory opinions 2019–2026 citing § 5-14-3-8 (17 opinions read); PAC HEA 1360 Overview; Indiana has no administrative-code fee rule for public records (APRA delegates no rulemaking except IDOA's state-agency uniform copying fee, § 8(c)). Nothing found on this item.

KS.snippet: If the agency has made reasonable efforts to contact the requester under subsection (e) and the requester fails to respond by the end of the third business day, the request is deemed withdrawn until the requester makes s

verified.source_language: If a public agency has made reasonable efforts to contact the requester pursuant to this section and the requester has failed to respond by the end of the third business day, the records request will be deemed to be withdrawn until a subsequent contact has been made by the requester to the public agency. … A public agency may charge and require advance payment of a fee for providing access to or furnishing copies of public records, subject to K.S.A. 45-219.
verified.effective_status: Amended effective 2025-07-01 (L. 2025, ch. 89, § 1 [HB 2134]); no 2026 amendment
verified.notes: KORA has no 'withdrawn after N days of nonpayment' clock and no prior-debt prepayment rule. Shape the engine must express: (1) the agency may withhold access/copies until advance payment is made (KS-0043); (2) the only deemed-withdrawal trigger is requester silence for 3 business days after the agency's cost-mitigation contact (KS-0042), which is reversible on subsequent requester contact. Nonpayment per se is otherwise unaddressed — a city's own procedures under 45-220(a) may fill this.

LA.snippet: The custodian need not provide copies where the requester fails to pay applicable copying fees after advance notice of the amount, or has an outstanding balance from a prior request.

verified.value: nonpayment after advance notice of amount excuses production; outstanding balance from a prior request excuses production; no N-day withdrawal period
verified.source_language: For all public records, except public records of state agencies, it shall be the duty of the custodian of the public records to provide copies to persons so requesting, unless the requestor fails to pay the applicable copying fees after being notified of the amount in advance of production or the requestor has an outstanding balance from a prior request.
verified.effective_status: Current (last amended Acts 2024, No. 411; fee text of (C)(1)(a) as amended by Acts 2023, No. 247, eff. Aug. 1, 2023; no 2025 or 2026 amendment found)
verified.notes: Two nonpayment consequences, both discretionary excuses of the copy duty: (1) failure to pay after advance notice, (2) outstanding balance from a prior request (prior-debt gate). No statutory deemed-withdrawal clock. Identical language for state agencies in 44:32(C)(2)(a).

MA.snippet: A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the RAO responded to the requestor within 10 business days under subsection (b).

MI.snippet: A fee for search, examination, review, and separation/deletion of exempt material may not be charged unless failure to charge would result in unreasonably high costs to the public body because of the nature of the reques

MO.snippet: A request is considered withdrawn if the requester fails to remit all fees within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars.

verified.source_language: Every custodian of public records shall permit any record in the custodian's custody to be inspected and examined at reasonable times and under reasonable supervision by any person, and shall, as promptly as possible, furnish copies thereof upon payment of any fees as may be prescribed by law.
verified.effective_status: Current (ncleg.gov General Statutes current through S.L. 2026-30; § 132-6.2 last amended S.L. 2004-129 — no 2024, 2025 or 2026 amendment; no pending 2026 modification listed for §§ 132-6, 132-6.2, 132-1.4A(l), 132-10)
verified.notes: No withdrawal-after-N-days rule and no prior-debt prepayment rule. Nonpayment simply means the copy-furnishing duty (conditioned 'upon payment') is not yet triggered. Searched: N.C. Gen. Stat. ch. 132 (Public Records) in full at ncleg.gov (current through S.L. 2026-30), incl. §§ 132-1(b), 132-6, 132-6.1, 132-6.2, 132-1.4A(l), 132-10; ch. 159 (§ 159-32.1); ncleg 'Law modifications not yet reflected in statute' (2026); N.C. Attorney General 2019 Open Government Guide (ncdoj.gov, 'Charging Fees' section); Governor's Office 'Guidance for Public Records and Meetings Access' (July 2018); ncdoj.gov Legal Opinions Directory (search 'public records fee' — no fee opinion surfaced; the 'Public Records' opinion page returned a WordPress error); no N.C. Administrative Code title governs municipal public-records fees (agency-specific NCAC fee rules exist only for the promulgating agency).

NE.snippet: If the requester does not respond to the custodian within ten business days of the cost estimate, the custodian shall not proceed to fulfill the request.

verified.unit: business days after the cost estimate without a requester response → custodian shall not proceed (request lapses); prior-debt prepayment: silent
verified.source_language: The requester shall have ten business days to review the estimated costs, including any special service charge, and request the custodian to fulfill the original request, negotiate with the custodian to narrow or simplify the request, or withdraw the request. If the requester does not respond to the custodian within ten business days, the custodian shall not proceed to fulfill the request.
verified.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
verified.notes: The statutory consequence attaches to nonresponse to the ESTIMATE, not to nonpayment as such: 'If the requester does not respond to the custodian within ten business days, the custodian shall not proceed to fulfill the request.' No withdrawal-after-N-days-of-nonpayment rule and no prior-unpaid-balance prepayment rule in statute or AG guidance.

verified.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1) (retrieval window only); GRC custodian FAQ
verified.source_language: A requestor shall have 14 business days to retrieve the government records following notice from the custodian that the request has been completed and the records are available.
verified.effective_status: Current (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5 last amended P.L.2024, c.16, s.2, effective 2024-09-03; official codified text checked 2026-08-18 shows no later amendment)

(Jan 2025); GRC custodian FAQ; GRC official OPRA request form (2024-9-3); GRC Custodian's Toolkit (2011); GRC Special Service Charge 14-point analysis; OPRA Alerts Vol.2 Iss.2 and Vol.3 Iss.2. verified.unit: days after copy reproduced (unclaimed copy may be disposed of)
verified.source_authority: Nev. Admin. Code § 239.868(2) (Executive Department agencies only)
verified.source_language: If a person who requests to receive a copy of a public record does not claim the copy, the records official may dispose of the copy if the person does not: (a) Claim the copy from the agency; or (b) Notify the agency of when the person will claim the copy, within 30 days after the copy is reproduced.
verified.effective_status: Current
verified.notes: No withdrawal-after-N-days or prior-debt provision for any body. Agency regime: unclaimed copies may be disposed of if not claimed (or a pickup date notified) within 30 days after reproduction.

verified.value: not_fulfilled_until_paid; notice of amount due required first; no statutory withdrawal period
verified.source_authority: Ohio Attorney General, 2026 Ohio Sunshine Laws: An Open Government Resource Manual, ch. 2, § 12 'Copies, and delivery or transmission, "at cost"' (pp. 21-22) (citing Call v. Fragale 2004-Ohio-6589; Ware v. Akron 2021-Ohio-624)
verified.source_language: There is no obligation to provide free copies to someone who cannot or will not pay. However, before denying a request for failure to pay, the public office must first inform the requester of the amount due.
verified.effective_status: Current (2026 manual edition)
verified.notes: No N-day withdrawal rule and no prior-debt prepayment rule in Ohio law. Consequence of nonpayment: copies are not furnished (Manual: no obligation to provide free copies), but the office must first state the amount due.

OK.snippet: If a request is solely for a commercial purpose, or would clearly cause excessive disruption of the body's essential functions, the body may charge a reasonable fee to recover the direct cost of record search and copying

OR.snippet: If the requester fails to pay the fee within 60 days of being informed of the fee (or within 60 days of denial of a fee waiver), the public body shall close the request.

verified.unit: days after the agency's response (statute says 'days', not 'business days') — unretrieved copies may be disposed of and fees paid to date retained; plus prior-debt rule: access on a new request may be withheld until fees for earlier requests are paid
verified.source_authority: 65 P.S. § 67.905; OOR Advisory Opinion Jan. 12, 2016 (applying Dep't of Transp. v. Drack, 42 A.3d 355 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2012)); § 67.902(a)(6)
verified.source_language: If an agency response to a requester states that copies of the requested records are available for delivery at the office of an agency and the requester fails to retrieve the records within 60 days of the agency's response, the agency may dispose of any copies which have not been retrieved and retain any fees paid to date.
verified.effective_status: Current — § 1307 unamended since enactment (Act 3 of 2008); compiled text reflects amendments through Act 29 of 2023; no 2024–2026 enacted amendment to §§ 901–905 or 1307 found
verified.notes: Three operative pieces: (1) 60-day discard of unretrieved copies with fees retained (§ 905); (2) refusal to pay is an extension ground with a 30-day outer limit, then deemed denied (§ 902(a)(6), (b)(2)); (3) prior unpaid fees may block access on later requests but not the duty to respond timely (OOR AO 2016). No 'deemed withdrawn after N days' rule.

verified.source_language: If a deposit as provided in subsection (B) is required by the public body, the record must be furnished or made available for inspection or copying no later than thirty calendar days from the date on which the deposit is received, unless the records are more than twenty-four months old, in which case the public body has no later than thirty-five calendar days from the date on which the deposit was received to fulfill the request. The full amount of the total cost must be paid at the time of the production of the request.
verified.effective_status: Current (2017 Act No. 67, eff. May 19, 2017; no later amendment through 2025 session; no 2026 act found)
verified.notes: No withdrawal-after-N-days, no prior-debt prepayment rule. Practical effect of SC-0026: if a permitted deposit is never paid the production clock never starts, but the statute prescribes no lapse or closure action. Searched: S.C. Code Title 30 ch. 4 (FOIA, all sections; fee content confined to § 30-4-30(B)-(C)); S.C. Code of Regulations index and ch. 12 (Archives & History) — no FOIA fee regulation exists; SC Attorney General FOIA page and opinion search (scag.gov/search: 'FOIA fee 30-4-30', 'prorated hourly salary', 'prevailing commercial rate', 'FOIA redaction fee') — opened AG Ops. of June 28, 2019 (Forrest/Hudson), Jan. 24, 2020 (McCurdy, clerks of court), May 31, 2024 (Swindler, BWC); 2024, 2025 and 2026 Acts lists on scstatehouse.gov (no FOIA fee act); S. 6 (2025-2026) which re-states § 30-4-30(B) unchanged and remains in Senate Judiciary.

verified.value: prior_debt_bar_until_paid (entity not required to comply with ANY further request from the person until unpaid copies are paid; conditioned on a prior estimate the person agreed to); no statutory N-day withdrawal
verified.source_authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(vii)(b); OORC FAQ 'Are there penalties for failing to inspect or pay for copies of public records?'
verified.source_language: (b) If a person makes a request for copies of a public record and, after copies have been produced, the person fails to pay to the governmental entity the cost for producing such copies, the governmental entity is not required to comply with any public records request from the person until the person pays for such copies; provided, that the person was provided with an estimated cost for producing the copies in accordance with subdivision (a)(7)(B)(ii) prior to producing the copies and the person agreed to pay the estimated cost for such copies.
verified.effective_status: Current (FindLaw reproduction current through Jan. 2, 2024; OORC 2024 and 2025 Legislative Updates report no amendment to these provisions; 2026 session: no fee amendment found, OORC Fall 2026 update not yet published)
verified.notes: Applies to all governmental entities. The OORC FAQ (official) restates the clause verbatim and adds that where a requestor converts a copy request to inspection after copies were produced in reliance on an agreement, the entity 'may be entitled to seek equitable relief'. No withdrawal-after-N-days rule; city may set an abandonment window in policy.

verified.value: withdrawn_after_days: 60 | prior_debt_prepayment_threshold_usd: 100 | deposit_nonpayment: withdrawn after 10 business days
verified.unit: calendar days after the requestor is informed of charges (or after records made available) | USD unpaid on prior requests permitting a deposit/bond and barring other collection | business days
verified.source_language: (e) A request is considered to have been withdrawn if the requestor fails to inspect or duplicate the public information in the offices of the governmental body on or before the 60th day after the date the information is made available or fails to pay the postage and any other applicable charges accrued under Subchapter F on or before the 60th day after the date the requestor is informed of the charges. [§ 552.263(c):] An officer for public information or the officer's agent may require a deposit or bond for payment of unpaid amounts owing to the governmental body in relation to previous requests that the requestor has made under this chapter before preparing a copy of public information in response to a new request if those unpaid amounts exceed $100. The officer for public information or the officer's agent may not seek payment of those unpaid amounts through any other means.
verified.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
verified.notes: TX-0035's clause is corrected to § 552.263(c) by TX-9003. School districts have an additional 180-day prepayment rule (§ 552.2661) — not municipal.

verified.value: prior_debt_prepayment: after an invoice is sent and the requester has not paid fees from a previous request, the entity may require payment of past fees and future estimated fees before beginning to process the new request; no withdrawal-after-N-days rule
verified.source_language: (8)(a) A governmental entity may require payment of past fees and future estimated fees before beginning to process a request if: (i) fees are expected to exceed $50; or (ii) after the government entity has sent an invoice, the requester has not paid fees from a previous request. (b) Any prepaid amount in excess of fees due shall be returned to the requester.
verified.effective_status: Current (63G-2-203 last amended Ch. 33 (S.B. 188), 2025 General Session, effective 3/17/2025 — technical wording change to (8)(a)(ii) only; no 2026 General Session amendment as of 2026-08-19)
verified.notes: Prior-debt prepayment is expressly authorized (any amount — the $50 threshold does not apply to the prior-debt prong). No statutory deemed-withdrawal or lapse period for nonpayment; the request simply is not processed until prepayment. Cities may add lapse rules by ordinance/policy under § 63G-2-203(3)(c) and § 63G-2-701(4).

WA.snippet: If the requester fails to inspect, pay for, or claim an installment of a records request, the agency need not fulfill the balance of the request.

citations: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
AL.snippet: For a time-intensive request, the public officer shall require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before providing a substantive response.

verified.value: production presumption clock starts only on payment of the estimated fees (30 business/60 calendar days standard; 180 business/270 calendar days time-intensive); no grace period; no lapse action
verified.source_language: There shall be a rebuttable presumption that a proper standard request has been denied by the public officer if: a. A substantive response is not provided to the standard request within the earlier of 30 business days or 60 calendar days following acknowledgment of receipt by the public officer; or b. The public records are not produced within the earlier of 30 business days or 60 calendar days following the payment of the estimated fees to the public officer. | (b)(6) ... b. The records are not produced within the earlier of 180 business days or 270 calendar days following the payment of the estimated fees to the public officer.
verified.effective_status: Current; Act 2024-278 effective October 1, 2024; no amendment to the fee provisions in the 2025 or 2026 Regular Sessions (codified history through Act 2026-592 shows only Act 2024-278)
verified.notes: While the estimated fee is unpaid the production-side denial presumption has not started; the substantive-response clock (15 business days from acknowledgment; 45 business days from election to proceed) is separate. For time-intensive requests the officer 'shall withhold any substantive response until receipt of payment', so an unpaid mandatory fee also stalls the substantive response. No grace/lapse rule. Official link is the Legislature's Code of Alabama viewer (browse Title 36 > Chapter 12 > Article 3; section text also served by its GraphQL endpoint https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql, query codeOfAlabamaSection); alternate direct text: enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF.

AZ.snippet: The custodian may require a person requesting a mailed copy to pay in advance for any copying and postage charges.

verified.source_language: The custodian may require any person requesting that the custodian mail a copy of any public record to pay in advance for any copying and postage charges. [§ 39-121.01(E):] Access to a public record is deemed denied if a custodian fails to promptly respond to a request for production of a public record or fails to provide to the requesting person an index of any record or categories of records that are withheld from production pursuant to subsection D, paragraph 2 of this section.
verified.effective_status: Amended effective September 26, 2025 (Laws 2025, ch. 102, SB 1372, approved May 2, 2025; general effective date of the 57th Leg., 1st Reg. Sess.) — codified text opened at azleg.gov 2026-08-19
verified.notes: Arizona has no numeric response clock (only 'promptly', with deemed denial for failure to promptly respond) and no provision that an unpaid advance payment tolls, pauses or affects it; no grace period; no lapse action. If the agency determines that the request seeks disclosable public records, the agency shall also state the estimated date and time when the records will be made available.

verified.source_language: Upon request for records transmission by a person seeking a copy of any public record, the custodian shall transmit a copy of the record by United States mail, other delivery service, facsimile, or electronic mail. No transmission fees may be charged to the record requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail. Within the period specified in section 24-72-203 (3)(a), the custodian shall notify the record requester that a copy of the record is available but will only be sent to the requester once the custodian either receives payment or makes arrangements for receiving payment for all costs associated with records transmission and for all other fees lawfully allowed, unless recovery of all or any portion of such costs or fees has been waived by the custodian. Upon either receiving such payment or making arrangements to receive such payment at a later date, the custodian shall send the record to the requester as soon as practicable but no more than three business days after receipt of, or making arrangements to receive, such payment.

verified.source_language: In any instance in which an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 for responding to a request, the agency shall notify the requester within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days and inform the requester of the estimate of the costs, and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs. In any instance in which the estimated costs for production of the records exceeds $500.00, an agency may insist on prepayment of the costs prior to beginning search, retrieval, review, or production of the records. AL.snippet: If the public officer elects to charge a fee for a standard request, the officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment.

verified.source_language: Records requested: (Be as specific as possible. A public officer is not obligated to respond to a request that is vague, ambiguous, overly broad, or unreasonable in scope, nor is a public officer obligated to respond to a request that seeks records that do not exist or materials that are not public records. Additionally, extensive requests for public records may increase the fees to cover the administrative cost of searching and copying the requested records.) [...] Payment of fees may be required before your request is fulfilled.
verified.effective_status: Current; Act 2024-278 effective October 1, 2024; no amendment to the fee provisions in the 2025 or 2026 Regular Sessions (codified history through Act 2026-592 shows only Act 2024-278)
verified.notes: No overrun/re-issue rule (no revised-estimate duty, no collection block, no restarted window). The default form's 'may increase the fees' warning is notice text, not a re-issue procedure. Official link is the Legislature's Code of Alabama viewer (browse Title 36 > Chapter 12 > Article 3; section text also served by its GraphQL endpoint https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/graphql, query codeOfAlabamaSection); alternate direct text: enrolled Act 2024-278 PDF.

verified.source_authority: Ariz. Rev. Stat. Title 39, ch. 1, art. 2
verified.source_language: The custodian of such records shall promptly furnish such copies, printouts or photographs and may charge a fee if the facilities are available, except that public records for purposes listed in section 39-122 or 39-127 shall be furnished without charge.
verified.effective_status: Amended effective September 26, 2025 (Laws 2025, ch. 102, SB 1372, approved May 2, 2025; general effective date of the 57th Leg., 1st Reg. Sess.) — codified text opened at azleg.gov 2026-08-19

verified.source_language: Except with respect to public records exempt from disclosure by express provisions of law, each state or local agency, upon a request for a copy of records that reasonably describes an identifiable record or records, shall make the records promptly available to any person upon payment of fees covering direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if applicable. Upon request, an exact copy shall be provided unless impracticable to do so.

verified.source_authority: C.R.S. § 24-72-205; Legislative Council Staff CORA summary
verified.source_language: Before completing a request that will take more than one hour of research and retrieval time, the custodian may require the requestor to pay a deposit equal to the estimated staff time needed to comply with the request. If the actual time spent turns out to be more or less than the initial estimate, the custodian may require an additional payment or make a partial refund of the deposit, respectively.
verified.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
verified.notes: No statutory overrun/re-issue rule. Legislative Council guidance (not law) says the custodian 'may require an additional payment or make a partial refund' when actual time differs from the estimate; nothing about blocking collection or restarting a window. GA.snippet: Where an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 to respond, it shall notify the requester within three business days and inform the requester of the cost estimate.

verified.source_language: In any instance in which an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 for responding to a request, the agency shall notify the requester within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days and inform the requester of the estimate of the costs, and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs.
verified.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
verified.notes: No rule requiring a revised estimate on overrun, blocking collection above the estimate (other than (c)(3)'s 'lawfully estimated and agreed to' limit), or restarting any window. KS.snippet: Upon request, the agency shall provide an itemized statement of costs charged to the requester, including the hourly rates for each employee involved and an itemized list of any other fees.

verified.source_language: Upon request, a public agency shall provide to the person requesting access to or copies of public records pursuant to this section an itemized statement of costs incurred by the public agency and charged to such requester. Such itemized statement shall include, but not be limited to, the hourly rates charged for each employee involved in making the requested records available and an itemized list of any other fees charged to provide access to or furnish copies of the requested records. … When the staff time needed to respond to a records request will exceed five hours or the estimated actual cost for staff time needed to fill the request exceeds $200, the public agency shall make reasonable efforts to contact the requester and engage in interactive communication about mitigating costs to fill the request. The requester is not obligated to mitigate costs.
verified.effective_status: Amended effective 2025-07-01 (L. 2025, ch. 89, § 1 [HB 2134]); no 2026 amendment
verified.notes: No overrun/re-issue rule (no revised-estimate requirement, no collection bar, no window restart). The prior '$200' figure belongs to the cost-mitigation trigger, not to a re-issue rule. Interplay only: if a revised estimate of staff-time cost crosses $200 (or 5 hours), the (e)(1) mandatory contact duty attaches. Itemized statement of actual costs on request ((c)(4)). verified.source_language: For all public records, except public records of state agencies, it shall be the duty of the custodian of the public records to provide copies to persons so requesting, unless the requestor fails to pay the applicable copying fees after being notified of the amount in advance of production or the requestor has an outstanding balance from a prior request.
verified.effective_status: Current (last amended Acts 2024, No. 411; fee text of (C)(1)(a) as amended by Acts 2023, No. 247, eff. Aug. 1, 2023; no 2025 or 2026 amendment found)

MI.snippet: A public body's procedures must use a standard form for detailed itemization of any fee that clearly lists and explains the allowable charges for each of the six fee components used in estimating or charging.

MO.snippet: A requester may request an estimate of the cost of copies before the public body produces them.

NE.snippet: With its timely response, the custodian must provide the requester an estimate of the expected cost of the copies.

verified.source_language: Upon receipt of a written request for access to or copies of a public record, the custodian of such record shall provide to the requester as soon as is practicable and without delay, but not more than four business days after actual receipt of the request, an estimate of the expected cost of the copies and either (a) access to or, if copying equipment is reasonably available, copies of the public record, (b) if there is a legal basis for denial of access or copies, a written denial of the request together with the information specified in section 84-712.04, or (c) if the entire request cannot with reasonable good faith efforts be fulfilled within four business days after actual receipt of the request due to the significant difficulty or the extensiveness of the request, a written explanation, including the earliest practicable date for fulfilling the request, an estimate of the expected cost of any copies, and an opportunity for the requester to modify or prioritize the items within the request.
verified.effective_status: Current — § 84-712 as amended by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, § 8 (operative three calendar months after the 2024 sine die adjournment, i.e., July 19, 2024; LB 43 § 22); codified source line ends 'Laws 2024, LB43, § 8'; 2025–2026 session-law search found only amendments to the exemption section § 84-712.05 (LB 525, LB 1096, approved April 2026), none to the fee, deposit, estimate or waiver subsections.
verified.notes: No overrun / revised-estimate re-issue rule; nothing blocks collection above the estimate or restarts the ten-business-day window on a revised estimate. verified.source_language: The requestor shall have the opportunity to review and object to any fee or charge prior to it being incurred. There shall be a rebuttable presumption that the fees or charges presented by the custodian are reasonable. If the requestor objects to the fees or charges, the burden of proof shall be on the requestor to demonstrate that the fees or charges are unreasonable.

NY.snippet: The requester shall be informed of the estimated cost of preparing the copy if more than two hours of employee time is needed or if an outside professional service would be retained.

verified.value: video: no revised estimate; overrun (max 20%) collectible on fulfillment only if advance notice given; general records: no rule
verified.source_language: If the actual cost exceeds the estimated actual cost, a state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office may charge a requester for the difference upon fulfilling a request for video records if the requester is notified in advance that the actual cost may be up to twenty per cent higher than the estimated actual cost. A state or local law enforcement agency or a prosecuting attorney's office shall not charge a requester a difference that exceeds twenty per cent of the estimated actual cost.
verified.effective_status: Current (video-record cost language added eff. April 9, 2025 by H.B. 315, 135th G.A.; carried unchanged in the Sept. 30, 2025 (H.B. 96) and Sept. 7, 2026 (H.B. 31) versions)

The advance notice ('actual cost may be up to twenty per cent higher') is a gate on collecting any overrun; nothing restarts a window. No overrun rule exists for non-video municipal records.

AL.snippet: A public officer may require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before the requester may receive any public records (standard request); more generally, a certified copy is furnished on paymen

verified.source_language: The public officer may require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before the requester may receive any public records. If the public officer elects to charge a fee, the public officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment. The requester may opt not to pay the fee and thus not receive any substantive response. Additionally, the public officer shall have the discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records. | § 36-12-43(a): It is the policy of the state to promptly provide residents with the opportunity to inspect public records and to request a copy, subject to payment of reasonable fees ...

verified.source_language: Arizona's public records law allows a public body to impose copying fees in response to public records requests for noncommercial purposes. Under that law, a public body can impose copying fees to offset copying costs only when a requesting party asks the public body to furnish copies of records. A public body should not impose copying fees on a party making a public records request when the requesting party asks only to inspect records or uses a personal device to make his or her own copies.
verified.effective_status: Current (opinion 2013; handbook rev. 2018, posted 2025)
verified.notes: No request-level dollar maximum. Non-commercial fees are bounded to copying (and postage) costs; commercial charges (§ 39-121.03(A)) may include market value and are unbounded. Under any such policy, the custodian shall not impose a charge for the first hour of time expended in connection with the research and retrieval of public records. After the first hour of time has been expended, the custodian may charge a fee for the research and retrieval of public records that shall not exceed thirty dollars per hour.

verified.value: shall not exceed the cost thereof to the public agency (computer-stored copies); paper copies capped per page only
verified.source_language: The fee for any copy provided in accordance with subsection (a) of section 1-211 shall not exceed the cost thereof to the public agency. || 35. The provisions of §1-212, G.S., set forth all permissible fees that an agency may charge in connection with providing copies of public records. See §1-212(a), G.S., ("[t]he fee for any copy provided in accordance with the [FOI] Act.") (Emphasis added); see also §1-212(b), G.S., ("[t]he fee for any copy provided in accordance with subsection (a) of section 1-211. . . .") (Emphasis added). 36. In the context of non-computer-stored records (i.e. paper records), the explicit terms of §§1-212(a)(A) and (B), G.S., limit permissible fees to copying fees of twenty-five cents per page for state agencies and fifty cents per page for all other public agencies. 37. It is clear, therefore, that the fees a public agency may charge for paper records are solely derived from the costs attributable to providing the records in the prescribed medium. As an agency would not be able to provide original versions of paper records to requestors, they must make physical copies of such records to provide them to requestors. In the case of paper records, the physical copy is the prescribed medium in which the agency is obligated to provide records. Notably, nothing in §1-212(a), G.S., would permit the respondents to charge a fee for (or predicate their fee estimate on) any of the labor costs identified in paragraph 33, above.
verified.effective_status: Current — Gen. Stat. rev. to Jan. 1, 2025; § 1-212 not in the 2026 Supplement (rev. to Jan. 1, 2026 — only § 1-210(b)(17) amended in 2025); last amended P.A. 12-205; 2026-session public acts (through P.A. 26-68) searched — none amend § 1-212
verified.notes: There is no request-level statutory maximum; the ceilings are per-page ($0.50 municipal) for paper and 'cost to the public agency' (closed component list) for computer-stored copies, and § 1-212 is exhaustive — no other fee may be added (FIC 2025-0213 ¶ 35).

verified.source_language: (d) If the nature or volume of public records requested to be inspected or copied pursuant to this subsection is such as to require extensive use of information technology resources or extensive clerical or supervisory assistance by personnel of the agency involved, or both, the agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplication, a special service charge, which shall be reasonable and shall be based on the cost incurred for such extensive use of information technology resources or the labor cost of the personnel providing the service that is actually incurred by the agency or attributable to the agency for the clerical and supervisory assistance required, or both. || Providing access to public records is a statutory duty imposed by the Legislature upon all record custodians and should not be considered a profit-making or revenue-generating operation. AGO 85-03. Thus, public information must be open for inspection without charge unless otherwise expressly provided by law. See State ex rel. Davis v. McMillan, 38 So. 666 (Fla. 1905). See also AGOs 84-03 and 76-34 (only those fees or charges which are authorized by statute may be imposed upon an individual seeking access to public records).

IN.snippet: For a local public agency, the fiscal body of the political subdivision establishes the copying fee schedule by ordinance, and the fee must be uniform.

verified.source_language: This subsection applies to a public agency that is not a state agency. The fiscal body (as defined in IC 36-1-2-6) of the public agency, or the governing body, if there is no fiscal body, shall establish a fee schedule for the certification or copying of documents. The fee for certification of documents may not exceed five dollars ($5) per document. The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of: (1) ten cents ($0.10) per page for copies that are not color copies or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for color copies; or (2) the actual cost to the agency of copying the document. As used in this subsection, "actual cost" means the cost of paper and the per-page cost for use of copying or facsimile equipment and does not include labor costs or overhead costs. A fee established under this subsection must be uniform throughout the public agency and uniform to all purchasers.

NC.snippet: An agency may not charge a fee for an uncertified copy of a public record that exceeds the actual cost to the agency of making the copy.

verified.rule_type: Prohibition (fee may not exceed actual cost)
verified.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, no public agency shall charge a fee for an uncertified copy of a public record that exceeds the actual cost to the public agency of making the copy. For purposes of this subsection, "actual cost" is limited to direct, chargeable costs related to the reproduction of a public record as determined by generally accepted accounting principles and does not include costs that would have been incurred by the public agency if a request to reproduce a public record had not been made. || Therefore, it is the policy of this State that the people may obtain copies of their public records and public information free or at minimal cost unless otherwise specifically provided by law. verified.source_language: The public body may establish and collect reasonable fees not to exceed the actual cost of the search, retrieval, and redaction of records. The records must be furnished at the lowest possible cost to the person requesting the records. Fees charged by a public body must be uniform for copies of the same record or document and may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies.
verified.effective_status: Current (2017 Act No. 67, eff. May 19, 2017; no later amendment through 2025 session; no 2026 act found)
verified.notes: No dollar maximum. Two soft standards stack: actual cost (labor components) and prevailing commercial rate (copies), plus 'lowest possible cost'.

TN.snippet: When assessing fees for copies, records custodians shall utilize the most economical and efficient method of producing the requested records.

verified.value: “reasonable costs incurred in producing the requested material” — no request-level dollar cap; per-page ceilings under the schedule; anything above requires documented actual cost; excessive fees shall not hinder access
verified.source_authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)(i); § 8-4-604(a)(1)(A)(ii)(b); OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.C, § II.C
verified.source_language: (B)(i) A records custodian may require a requestor to pay the custodian's reasonable costs incurred in producing the requested material and to assess the reasonable costs in the manner established by the office of open records counsel pursuant to § 8-4-604. (ii) The records custodian shall provide a requestor an estimate of the reasonable costs to provide copies of the requested material. [§ 8-4-604(a)(1)(A)(ii)(b):] That excessive fees and other rules shall not be used to hinder access to nonexempt public information; [Schedule § I.C:] Application of an adopted schedule of charges shall not be arbitrary. Additionally, excessive fees and other rules shall not be used to hinder access to public records.
verified.effective_status: Current (FindLaw reproduction current through Jan. 2, 2024; OORC 2024 and 2025 Legislative Updates report no amendment to these provisions; 2026 session: no fee amendment found, OORC Fall 2026 update not yet published)
verified.notes: The operative standard is 'reasonable costs incurred in producing' assessed per the OORC manner; the safe harbor makes schedule-consistent fees presumptively reasonable; unreasonable/unfounded costs can be treated as a denial reviewable under § 10-7-505 (OORC FAQ).

verified.source_language: The charges for providing copies of public information may not be excessive and may not exceed the actual cost of producing the information or for making public information that exists in a paper record available for inspection. A governmental body, other than an agency of state government, may determine its own charges for providing copies of public information and its own charge, deposit, or bond for making public information that exists in a paper record available for inspection but may not charge an amount that is greater than 25 percent more than the amount established by the attorney general unless the governmental body requests an exemption under Subsection (c).
verified.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
verified.notes: No dollar request-level maximum. Three ceilings stack: (1) actual cost / not excessive; (2) for non-state bodies, each AG-established component + 25%; (3) the itemized-estimate cap of § 552.2615(d). TX-9002 amends TX-0027 with the verbatim clause.

UT.snippet: An entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover its actual cost of providing a record; the fee must be approved by the entity's executive officer.

verified.value: reasonable fee to cover the governmental entity's actual cost of providing a record
verified.unit: USD (request-level ceiling = actual cost, bounded by 'reasonable'; no statutory dollar maximum)
verified.source_language: (1)(a) Subject to Subsection (5), a governmental entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover the governmental entity's actual cost of providing a record. (b) A fee under Subsection (1)(a) shall be approved by the governmental entity's executive officer. | (2)(a) When a governmental entity compiles a record in a form other than that normally maintained by the governmental entity, the actual costs under this section may include the following: (i) the cost of staff time for compiling, formatting, manipulating, packaging, summarizing, or tailoring the record either into an organization or media to meet the person's request; (ii) the cost of staff time for search, retrieval, and other direct administrative costs for complying with a request; and (iii) in the case of fees for a record that is the result of computer output other than word processing, the actual incremental cost of providing the electronic services and products together with a reasonable portion of the costs associated with formatting or interfacing the information for particular users, and the administrative costs as set forth in Subsections (2)(a)(i) and (ii).
verified.effective_status: Current (63G-2-203 last amended Ch. 33 (S.B. 188), 2025 General Session, effective 3/17/2025 — technical wording change to (8)(a)(ii) only; no 2026 General Session amendment as of 2026-08-19)

Actual-cost components are enumerated in (2)(a) for compiled records; the executive officer must approve the fee ((1)(b)); fees fixed by other statutes are preserved ((9)). Applies to every governmental entity incl. political subdivisions.

verified.source_language: Labor and overhead costs are specifically excluded from the calculation of actual cost. The price of ink and paper is the cap to actual cost. Even then, given the practical cost of printing, agencies likely come out ahead if capping copies at $.10 per page. Chesterfield's fees are not justifiable or reasonable. In reality, the actual cost calculation comes into play only when copying unusually sized pieces of paper and postage costs to remote requesters. There is no need to use the actual cost calculation with standard size copies.

verified.source_language: Upon request for records transmission by a person seeking a copy of any public record, the custodian shall transmit a copy of the record by United States mail, other delivery service, facsimile, or electronic mail. No transmission fees may be charged to the record requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail. Within the period specified in section 24-72-203 (3)(a), the custodian shall notify the record requester that a copy of the record is available but will only be sent to the requester once the custodian either receives payment or makes arrangements for receiving payment for all costs associated with records transmission and for all other fees lawfully allowed, unless recovery of all or any portion of such costs or fees has been waived by the custodian. Upon either receiving such payment or making arrangements to receive such payment at a later date, the custodian shall send the record to the requester as soon as practicable but no more than three business days after receipt of, or making arrangements to receive, such payment.
verified.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)

verified.source_language: 59. In Stedman, the Commission found that: the superintendent printed out the potentially responsive emails because it was easier for her to read them that way, rather than on her computer, and because she believed that some of the emails might need to be redacted. Although the Commission appreciates that it may be easier for some people to review emails when they are in printed form, as opposed to reading them on a computer screen, the FOI Act does not permit a public agency to charge a fee for a copy of a nonexempt electronic record, when the requestor has asked that such record be provided electronically. The Commission takes administrative notice of the fact that there is no cost associated with transmitting a record electronically. (Emphasis added). Id. at ¶ 18. 60. [...] Id. at n. 2. ("The Commission notes, however, that if a public agency receives a request for a copy of, or to inspect a record that contains information that is required by law to be redacted, and the public agency must make a copy of the record in order to redact such information, the public agency may charge the requestor the statutory fee for that copy.") (Emphasis in original). 61. Additionally, such records were requested to be produced in an electronic format (specifically, email). Therefore, the District was not required to print out the records to provide them in the medium requested. Id. ("Accordingly it is concluded that the respondents violated §§1-211(a) and 1-212(b), G.S., by charging the complainant a copy fee of $.25 per page for unredacted paper copies, rather than providing them to her electronically, free of charge as she requested.") (Emphasis added).

IN.snippet: The fee for certification of documents may not exceed five dollars ($5) per document.

verified.source_language: This subsection applies to a public agency that is not a state agency. The fiscal body (as defined in IC 36-1-2-6) of the public agency, or the governing body, if there is no fiscal body, shall establish a fee schedule for the certification or copying of documents. The fee for certification of documents may not exceed five dollars ($5) per document. The fee for copying documents may not exceed the greater of: (1) ten cents ($0.10) per page for copies that are not color copies or twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for color copies; or (2) the actual cost to the agency of copying the document. As used in this subsection, "actual cost" means the cost of paper and the per-page cost for use of copying or facsimile equipment and does not include labor costs or overhead costs. A fee established under this subsection must be uniform throughout the public agency and uniform to all purchasers.

verified.effective_status: Current (2026 manual edition)
verified.notes: The Public Records Act neither requires certified copies nor sets a certification fee for municipal records. Where another statute sets a certified-copy fee for a specific record type it controls, and if the requester does not ask for certification only actual cost may be charged (Manual ch. 2 § 12, Call v. Fragale re R.C. 2303.20 — county clerk). Searched: R.C. 149.43 (all versions Oct. 24, 2024 through Sept. 7, 2026 on codes.ohio.gov, including the H.B. 315 (Apr. 9, 2025), H.B. 96 (Sept. 30, 2025) and H.B. 31 (Sept. 7, 2026) versions); R.C. 149.011, 109.43; the AG's 2026 Sunshine Laws Manual (fees ch. 2 §§ 11-13, policy ch. 7); the AG Model Public Records Policy; the AG index 'Opinions Interpreting Ohio's Sunshine Laws' (fee-related: 89-073, 99-012, 2001-012, 2014-009, 2022-018); State ex rel. Warren Newspapers v. Hutson (1994). Ohio has no administrative-code fee schedule for public records and no uniform state schedule; no municipal figure exists beyond 'at cost'.

verified.unit: USD per certified copy (city sets 'lawful fees' by ordinance/policy under the actual-cost standard)
verified.source_authority: Utah Code § 63G-2-201(6); § 63G-2-203(1)(a), (3)(c), (9); Archives payment form line 'Certification fee'
verified.source_language: (6) A governmental entity shall provide a person with a certified copy of a record if: (a) the person requesting the record has a right to inspect it; (b) the person identifies the record with reasonable specificity; and (c) the person pays the lawful fees. | (1)(a) Subject to Subsection (5), a governmental entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover the governmental entity's actual cost of providing a record. (b) A fee under Subsection (1)(a) shall be approved by the governmental entity's executive officer. | (3)(c) Political subdivisions shall establish fees by ordinance or written formal policy adopted by the governing body. | (9) This section does not alter, repeal, or reduce fees established by other statutes or legislative acts.
verified.effective_status: Current (63G-2-201 amended 2026 General Session, effective 7/1/2026; fee-related subsections (1)(a), (6), (8)(c), (10) unchanged in substance)
verified.notes: A certified copy must be provided when the requester has a right to inspect, identifies the record with reasonable specificity, and 'pays the lawful fees' (§ 63G-2-201(6)); GRAMA sets no certification figure and § 63G-2-203(9) preserves fees fixed by other statutes (none found for municipal records generally). The Archives official payment form has a 'Certification fee' line. Figure set locally. Utah sets no per-page or per-item figure for any public body. The state's binding constraint is the § 63G-2-203(1)(a) 'reasonable fee to cover ... actual cost' standard; the operative figure is set by the political subdivision by ordinance or written formal policy adopted by the governing body (§ 63G-2-203(3)(c)), and a political subdivision's GRAMA ordinance/policy must 'provide guidelines for establishment of fees in accordance with Section 63G-2-203' (§ 63G-2-701(3)(c)). Archives official form (2025): 'Additional fees are established by a local ordinance or policy'. State-agency fees are set through the budget process / § 63J-1-504 (§ 63G-2-203(3)(b)) — agency schedules (e.g., the annual State Agency Fees authorization acts, the AG office GRAMA fee schedule) do not bind municipalities.

verified.source_language: The public officer may require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before the requester may receive any public records. If the public officer elects to charge a fee, the public officer shall notify the requester of the estimated fee and withhold any public records until receipt of payment. The requester may opt not to pay the fee and thus not receive any substantive response. Additionally, the public officer shall have the discretion to require the requester to pay all or a portion of the estimated fee prior to searching for any responsive public records. | § 36-21-213(b): A custodial law enforcement agency may charge a reasonable fee for redaction and editing of a recording.

A county, a city, a town or any political subdivision of this state may take into consideration the following information when determining the amount of the onetime fee per copy: 1. The reasonable cost of reviewing, transmitting, making a copy of and, as necessary, redacting the video recording. 2. Any other relevant information.

verified.source_language: 37. It is found that the respondents arrived at the fee of $628.99 by using the hourly rate of the employee who was trained and charged with reviewing and redacting (i.e., pixelating and removing audio) from the requested video footage ($612) and copying such footage onto a flash drive ($16.99). 38. School Board of Manatee County, 135 So. 3d 560, 562 (Fla. 2d DCA 2014) (“An individual’s reason for requesting a public record is irrelevant”); Timoney v. City of Miami Civilian Investigative Panel, 917 So. 2d 885, 886n.3 (Fla. 3d DCA 2005) (“generally, a person’s motive in seeking access to public records is irrelevant”). || Providing access to public records is a statutory duty imposed by the Legislature upon all record custodians and should not be considered a profit-making or revenue-generating operation. verified.source_language: A public body may charge up to $10 for each hour spent by personnel in searching for and retrieving a requested record or examining the record for necessary redactions. No fees shall be charged for the first 8 hours spent by personnel in searching for or retrieving a requested record. A public body may charge the actual cost of retrieving and transporting public records from an off-site storage facility when the public records are maintained by a third-party storage company under contract with the public body. If a public body imposes a fee pursuant to this subsection (f), it must provide the requester with an accounting of all fees, costs, and personnel hours in connection with the request for public records. The provisions of this subsection (f) apply only to commercial requests.

verified.source_language: The custodian of such records shall promptly furnish such copies, printouts or photographs and may charge a fee if the facilities are available, except that public records for purposes listed in section 39-122 or 39-127 shall be furnished without charge. [§ 39-122(A):] A. No state, county or city, or any officer or board thereof shall demand or receive a fee or compensation for issuing certified copies of public records or for making search for them, when they are to be used in connection with a claim for a pension, allotment, allowance, compensation, insurance or other benefits which is to be presented to the United States or a bureau or department thereof. [§ 39-127(A):] A. A victim of a criminal offense that is a part I crime under the statewide uniform crime reporting program, the victim's attorney on behalf of the victim or an immediate family member of the victim if the victim is killed or incapacitated has the right to receive one copy of the police report, audio recordings and video recordings from the investigating law enforcement agency or charging prosecutorial agency at no charge and, on request of the victim, the court or the clerk of the court shall provide, at no charge, the minute entry or portion of the record of any proceeding in the case that arises out of the offense committed against the victim and that is reasonably necessary to pursue a claimed victim's right. [Ombudsman FAQ:] I requested copies of public records and cannot afford the copying fee. Must the public body waive the copying fee if it causes financial hardship? No. The law permits public bodies to impose a copying fee and does not require a waiver for financial hardship. That said, public bodies are not required to impose a charge for copies.

verified.source_language: Upon request for records transmission by a person seeking a copy of any public record, the custodian shall transmit a copy of the record by United States mail, other delivery service, facsimile, or electronic mail. No transmission fees may be charged to the record requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail. Within the period specified in section 24-72-203 (3)(a), the custodian shall notify the record requester that a copy of the record is available but will only be sent to the requester once the custodian either receives payment or makes arrangements for receiving payment for all costs associated with records transmission and for all other fees lawfully allowed, unless recovery of all or any portion of such costs or fees has been waived by the custodian. Upon either receiving such payment or making arrangements to receive such payment at a later date, the custodian shall send the record to the requester as soon as practicable but no more than three business days after receipt of, or making arrangements to receive, such payment. || If the public record is a result of computer output other than word processing, the fee for a copy, printout, or photograph thereof may be based on recovery of the actual incremental costs of providing the electronic services and products together with a reasonable portion of the costs associated with building and maintaining the information system. Such fee may be reduced or waived by the custodian if the electronic services and products are to be used for a public purpose, including public agency program support, nonprofit activities, journalism, and academic research. Fee reductions and waivers shall be uniformly applied among persons who are similarly situated. || Whenever a copy of any public record is required by the United States veterans administration or its successors or any other agency of the government of the United States to be used in determining the eligibility of any person who has served in the armed forces of the United States or any dependent of such person to participate in benefits for such person made available by the laws of the United States in relation to such service in the armed forces of the United States, the official charged with the custody of such public records, without charge, shall provide the applicant for such benefits or any person acting on his behalf, or the representative of such bureau or other agency, with a certified copy of such record.

verified.source_language: Documents shall be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge, as determined by the public body, if the person requesting the documents states the specific purpose for the request and indicates that a waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest. Waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest if the principal purpose of the request is to access and disseminate information regarding the health, safety and welfare or the legal rights of the general public and is not for the principal purpose of personal or commercial benefit. verified.source_language: A requester may not file multiple requests for public records solely to avoid payment of fees. When a public agency reasonably believes that one (1) or more requesters is segregating a request into a series of requests to avoid payment of fees authorized pursuant to this section, the public agency may aggregate such requests and charge the appropriate fees. verified.source_language: Under amendments to § 84-712(3)(c) contained in 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, for residents of Nebraska, the actual added cost used as the basis for calculation of a fee for copies of public records cannot include any charge for the existing salary or pay obligation to public officers or public employees with respect to the first eight cumulative hours of searching for, identifying, physically redacting, or copying public records responsive to a particular records request. A special service charge representing the time required in excess of eight cumulative hours to search for, identify, physically redact, and copy records responsive to a particular records request can be imposed for providing copies of public records, since a large records request may delay or otherwise disrupt the operation of the custodian's office.
verified.effective_status: Current — Attorney General 'Outline of Nebraska Public Records Statutes', marked Rev. 7/2024 (post-LB 43); official guidance / enforcement policy, not law.
verified.notes: No repeat-request carry-forward or cross-request aggregation rule. The eight-cumulative-hour allowance is per request as read by the AG Outline ('responsive to a particular records request'); nothing authorizes aggregating multiple requests from one requester to reach the threshold. Searched: Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 84-712 to 84-712.09 (full text of §§ 84-712, 84-712.01, 84-712.02, 84-712.03 opened on nebraskalegislature.gov); § 25-1280 (certified copies); § 13-609 (electronic payments); 2024 LB 43 slip law (opened, §§ 8–10, 22, 24–26); Attorney General 'Outline of Nebraska Public Records Statutes' (Rev. 7/2024, ago.nebraska.gov/public-records); AG opinions archive index (2003–2026); Nebraska has no administrative code chapter implementing the Public Records Statutes for political subdivisions and no statutory delegation of a fee figure to a rule-maker for local bodies (the only delegation, § 84-712(3)(e), is state-agency portal fees approved by the State Records Board).

verified.value: custodian not required to complete an identical request from the same requestor if the information has not changed (periodic requests for regularly updated records remain permitted); repeated requests to multiple custodians of the same agency while an identical/substantially similar request is pending may be denied; NO fee aggregation or carry-forward rule
verified.source_authority: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(i)(1) and (g), as amended by P.L.2024, c.16, s.2
verified.source_language: The custodian shall not be required to complete an identical request for access to a government record from the same requestor if the information has not changed. Nothing in this section shall prevent a requestor from filing periodic requests regarding regularly updated public records, including, but not limited to, certified payrolls, permits, and licensing applications. || Submission of repeated requests to multiple custodians in the same public agency for the same record, while an identical or substantially similar request is pending in the agency, shall permit the custodian to deny the request.
verified.effective_status: Current (N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5 last amended P.L.2024, c.16, s.2, effective 2024-09-03; official codified text checked 2026-08-18 shows no later amendment)
verified.notes: Repeat-request handling exists as access rules, not fee rules: no aggregation threshold, no unpaid-balance carry-forward. 47:1A-5.1 (court protective order for requestors intending to disrupt government function) is a judicial path, not a fee mechanism.

verified.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the policy may not limit the number of public records that the public office will make available to a single person, may not limit the number of public records that it will make available during a fixed period of time, and may not establish a fixed period of time before it will respond to a request for inspection or copying of public records, unless that period is less than eight hours.
verified.effective_status: Current (R.C. 149.43 as amended eff. Sept. 30, 2025, H.B. 96, 136th G.A.; a further amendment by H.B. 31, 136th G.A., eff. Sept. 7, 2026, is enacted-awaiting-effect and does not touch the fee/payment language)
verified.notes: No fee aggregation, carry-forward or aggregation threshold. The opposite constraint applies: a public records policy may not limit records per person or per period (OH-9018); the only per-requester volume rule is the ten-per-month DELIVERY cap for commercial-purpose requesters (OH-0024/OH-9006). Searched: R.C. 149.43 (all versions Oct. 24, 2024 through Sept. 7, 2026 on codes.ohio.gov, including the H.B. 315 (Apr. 9, 2025), H.B. 96 (Sept. 30, 2025) and H.B. 31 (Sept. 7, 2026) versions); R.C. 149.011, 109.43; the AG's 2026 Sunshine Laws Manual (fees ch. 2 §§ 11-13, policy ch. 7); the AG Model Public Records Policy; the AG index 'Opinions Interpreting Ohio's Sunshine Laws' (fee-related: 89-073, 99-012, 2001-012, 2014-009, 2022-018); State ex rel. Warren Newspapers v. Hutson (1994). Ohio has no administrative-code fee schedule for public records and no uniform state schedule; no municipal figure exists beyond 'at cost'.

verified.value: unpaid fees from an earlier request carry forward — the agency may withhold access on a new request until all fees, including those for earlier requests, are paid (still must respond/extend within 5 business days); no aggregation threshold; policies limiting the number of records or requests are prohibited (§ 1308(1); OOR AO Aug. 19, 2022)
verified.source_authority: OOR Advisory Opinion Jan. 12, 2016 (applying Dep't of Transp. v. Drack, 42 A.3d 355 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 2012)); 65 P.S. §§ 67.901, 67.905, 67.1308(1); OOR Advisory Opinion Aug. 19, 2022
verified.source_language: Section 901 of the RTKL permits an agency to process the request but to withhold access to the request until all applicable fees, including fees for earlier requests, are paid ... However, even if fees are owed in response to a prior RTKL request, agencies must still timely process future RTKL requests. [§ 1308:] A policy or regulation adopted under this act may not include any of the following: (1) A limitation on the number of records which may be requested or made available for inspection or duplication.
verified.effective_status: Current (advisory opinions; § 1308 unamended)
verified.notes: No repeat-request fee aggregation exists (and § 1308 forbids caps on records/requests). The only cross-request fee mechanic is the prior-debt access gate.

TN.snippet: A governmental entity's policy shall specify the number of requests within a calendar month that triggers aggregation; that amount must be no lower than four (4) requests.

verified.unit: requests per calendar month (aggregation trigger; entity sets the number at or above 4 in its policy; optional to aggregate)
verified.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests §§ I.B–E, II.A–D (delegated from Tenn. Code Ann. § 8-4-604(a)(2))
verified.source_language: D. A governmental entity's public record policy shall indicate the number of requests within a calendar month that will trigger aggregation; that amount must be no lower than four (4) requests. This amount is the aggregation threshold. ... A. Once a records custodian reaches the aggregation threshold, the records custodian is no longer required to deduct the labor threshold set forth in the Schedule of Reasonable Charges or any other minimum charge per request threshold that would ordinarily be waived. B. When the aggregation threshold is met, a records custodian choosing to aggregate requests must inform the requestor(s) of the determination to aggregate and of the right of the requestor(s) to appeal the records custodian's decision to aggregate to the OORC. C. Requests for current records that are routinely released and readily accessible, such as agendas or meeting minutes, are exempt from this policy.
verified.effective_status: Current; effective Jan. 20, 2017
verified.notes: No carry-forward/estimate-reuse rule for repeat requests; the state mechanism is aggregation: single requestor or multiple requestors acting in concert (coordinator determination), threshold ≥4/month set by policy, level (entity/department) set by policy, effect = free hour and other per-request minimum waivers need not be deducted, with notice + OORC appeal, routine records exempt. Delegation followed: § 8-4-604(a)(2) → OORC policy (opened).

verified.value: same_day_aggregation: all requests received in one calendar day from an individual MAY be treated as one request for cost calculation (not across individuals for an organization) | repeat_request: free certification of prior production in lieu of re-copying | prior_unpaid > $100: deposit/bond before new request | § 552.275 cumulative personnel time per requestor per month/year
verified.source_language: (e) Except as otherwise provided by this subsection, all requests received in one calendar day from an individual may be treated as a single request for purposes of calculating costs under this chapter. A governmental body may not combine multiple requests under this subsection from separate individuals who submit requests on behalf of an organization.
verified.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
verified.notes: No carry-forward of unused free allowance and no aggregation threshold beyond the same-calendar-day rule; the § 552.275 requestor ledger (if adopted) is the only cross-request counter.

verified.value: (a) fee carry-forward: a non-Utah-media requester who submitted a separate request within the 10 days before the current request loses the free first quarter hour (10-day look-back per requestor); (b) no fee aggregation threshold; related non-fee rules: entity need not fulfill a request that 'unreasonably duplicates prior records requests from that person' (§ 63G-2-201(7)(a)(iv)); a substantial number of records requested within five working days of each other is an 'extraordinary circumstance' extending the response clock (§ 63G-2-204(6)(c)(ii)); vexatious-requester relief (§ 63G-2-209)
verified.source_language: (5)(c) Notwithstanding Subsection (5)(b)(iii), a governmental entity is not prevented from charging a fee for the first quarter hour of staff time spent in responding to a request under Section 63G-2-204 if the person who submits the request: (i) is not a Utah media representative; and (ii) previously submitted a separate request within the 10-day period immediately before the date of the request to which the governmental entity is responding. | § 63G-2-201(7)(a): In response to a request, a governmental entity is not required to: ... (iv) fulfill a person's records request if the request unreasonably duplicates prior records requests from that person; | § 63G-2-204(6)(c)(ii): the requester seeks a substantial number of records or records series in requests filed within five working days of each other;
verified.effective_status: Current (63G-2-203 last amended Ch. 33 (S.B. 188), 2025 General Session, effective 3/17/2025 — technical wording change to (8)(a)(ii) only; no 2026 General Session amendment as of 2026-08-19)
verified.notes: The only fee-side repeat rule is the 10-day look-back that strips the free quarter hour from non-media repeat requesters (UT-0036). Utah has no cost-aggregation threshold across requests. The duplication, five-working-day clustering, and vexatious-requester provisions are processing/clock rules, not fee rules.
